On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Xú Dù, General Who Guards the North, was dispatched to lead troops to construct a city at the southern mouth of Wǎn.
At this time, there had been no rain for a long time.
On the *jǐngwǔ* day,
the imperial carriage proceeded to Zhōngshān Temple to sacrifice at the Temple of Emperor Jiǎng.
On that day, rain fell,
continuing until the end of the month.
In the fifth month, on the first day, *jǐngchén*,
there was a solar eclipse.
The officials reported: according to old ritual,
when appearing in the front hall,
one wears a crimson gauze robe and a *tōngtiānguān*.
An imperial edict stated:
“This was adopted by previous dynasties,
but my intention is different.
On the new moon, to assist the great sun,
the *gǔnmiǎn* ceremonial attire should be worn.
From now on,
this shall be the permanent standard.”
On the *jǐngyín* day,
the Kingdom of Fúnán sent envoys to present local products.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Xióng Tánlǎng, Governor of Běijiāng Prefecture, killed Commander Zhōu Wényù in the army,
and raised troops in revolt.
Wáng Lín dispatched his generals Cháng Zhòng'ài and Cáo Qìng to lead troops to assist Yú Xiàomài.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Yítóng Hóu Āndū defeated Zhòng'ài's forces at Zuǒlǐ,
capturing Lín's cousin Xí, commander Yáng Jiǎn, and over thirty others.
Zhòng'ài fled.
On Gēngyín,
the people of Lúshān slew him
and sent his head to the capital.
On Jiǎwǔ,
the victorious army returned.
An imperial edict stated:
"Tánlǎng's treasonous bite
is a crime beyond pardon.
I have commanded the various armies
to pursue and suppress him,
and he shall be decapitated and quartered
to clarify the laws and regulations."
Qian, Prince of Línchuān, was ordered to go to WǎnKǒu to establish fortifications,
with Qián Dàojí defending them.
On Dīngyǒu,
Gāozǔ fell ill.
He sent Jiān Tàizǎi and Shàngshū Zuǒ Púshè Wáng Tōng to report his illness to the Tàimiào,
and Jiān Tàizǎi and Zhōngshūlìng Xiè Zhé to report to the Dàshè and the northern and southern suburbs.
On Xīnchǒu,
Gāozǔ's illness slightly improved.
The coffin of the late Sīkōng Zhōu Wényù arrived from Jiànchāng.
On Rényín,
Gāozǔ, dressed in plain white, wept in the Eastern Hall,
his sorrow profound.
On Guǐmǎo,
Gāozǔ presided over a judicial inquiry into lawsuits.
〔二０〕That night,
Yínghuò was in Tiānzūn.
Gāozǔ's illness worsened again.
〔二一〕On Jǐngwǔ,
he passed away in the Xuánjī Palace,
at the age of fifty-seven.
His dying decree ordered Qian, Prince of Línchuān, to enter and succeed him.
On Jiǎyín,
the coffin of the Great Departed Emperor was moved for temporary burial to the western steps of the Tàijí Palace.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on Jiǎwǔ,
the ministers posthumously honored him with the title Emperor Wǔ,
with the temple name Gāozǔ.
On Jǐngshēn,
he was buried in Wàn'ānling.
Gāozǔ's wisdom brought peace to the populace,
and his martial prowess quelled chaos.
His brilliant strategies were unique,
surpassing all others,
thus he was able to conquer in all four directions,
suppress rebellions, and eliminate villains.
Upon ascending to the throne,
he assumed the responsibilities of a supreme minister,
always promoting lenient governance,
with love and nurture as his foundation.
Any demands for military provisions
were only made when absolutely necessary.
Furthermore, he led by example with frugality and simplicity;
his daily meals never exceeded a few dishes,
and for private banquets and gatherings,
all utensils were made of pottery and clam shells.
The dishes and delicacies
were merely sufficient,
without any wasteful extravagance.
Initially, after suppressing Hóu Jǐng
and establishing Shào Tài,
women, jade, and silks
were all distributed to the generals and soldiers.
Those who served in his inner chambers
wore clothes of unadorned colors,
and their ornaments contained no gold or kingfisher feathers.
Singers, bells, and female musicians
were not permitted in his presence.
After he ascended the throne,
he became even more rigorous in his humility and frugality.
Thus, his magnificent achievements and splendid virtues
brought glory to the empire.
Chén Lìbù Shàngshū Yáo Chá said: Gāozǔ's brilliant strategy and great magnanimity
allowed him to adapt to changes without limit,
surely a peer to Hàn Gāo [Liú Bāng] and Wèi Wǔ [Cáo Cāo].
When the Western Capital was overthrown,
his sincerity pierced heaven and man.
Wáng Sēngbiàn lacked the talent of Yī Yǐn
and merely harbored the resentment of Tónggōng;
Zhēnyáng relied on the dispatch of Qín's troops
without considering the tears of Mù Yíng.
Gāozǔ, however, stepped onto the mysterious path to govern a chaotic era,
seizing opportunities to rescue the drifting populace.
The foundation of kingship
began from this point.
How could it merely be confined to the victories of Kān Límín and Shēng Èr?
Thus, in an era of careful observance of seasons,
and a time of changing sounds and renewed things,
the common people returned with songs of praise,
and the fiery spirits departed as if relieved of a burden.
Compared to previous generations,
how splendid it was!
Collation Notes
Basic Annals Three: Shìzǔ
Shìzǔ, Emperor Wén, personal name Qiàn,
courtesy name Zǐhuá,
was the eldest son of Shǐxīng Zhāoliè Wáng.
In his youth, he was deeply astute and possessed insight and magnanimity,
with a handsome appearance.
He devoted himself to the classics and histories,
and his every action was refined and elegant,
always adhering to ritual and law, even in haste.
Gāozǔ loved him dearly,
often remarking,
"This child is the outstanding talent of my clan."
At the beginning of Liáng Tàiqīng,
he dreamt of two suns fighting,
one large and one small.
The larger one's light extinguished and it fell to the ground,
its color a true yellow,
and it was as large as a peck measure.
Shìzǔ then took one-third of it and embraced it.
During the Hóu Jǐng Rebellion,
many villagers relied on mountain lakes for banditry,
but Shìzǔ alone protected his family without committing any offenses.
As the chaos worsened day by day,
he fled to Lín'ān.
When Gāozǔ raised his righteous army,
Hóu Jǐng sent envoys to seize Shìzǔ and Héngyáng Xiàn Wáng.
Shìzǔ secretly hid a small knife in his sleeve,
hoping to harm Jǐng upon their meeting.
However, upon arrival, he was handed over to an official,
so his plan did not succeed.
When Gāozǔ's grand army besieged Shítou,
Jǐng intended to harm him repeatedly.
Coincidentally, Jǐng was defeated,
and Shìzǔ was able to escape and join Gāozǔ's camp.
He began his career as Prefect of Wúxīng.
At that time, the bandit leaders Jì Jī and Hǎo Zhòng of Xuānchéng each gathered over a thousand men,
invading and brutalizing the commandery.
Shìzǔ suppressed and pacified them.
In the second year of Chéngshèng,
he was granted the title of Xìnwǔ Jiāngjūn [General of Valiant Trust]
and was made Supervisor of Nánxú Prefecture.
In the third year,
when Gāozǔ campaigned north to Guǎnglíng,
he made Shìzǔ the vanguard,
and he won every battle.
When Gāozǔ was about to attack Wáng Sēngbiàn,
he first summoned Shìzǔ to consult with him.
At that time, Wáng Sēngbiàn's son-in-law, Dù Kān, occupied Wúxīng,
with a very strong army.
Gāozǔ secretly ordered Shìzǔ to return to Chángchéng
and establish barricades to prepare for Kān.
Shìzǔ's gathered troops numbered only a few hundred,
and he had few military provisions.
Kān sent his general Dù Tài with five thousand elite soldiers,
who took advantage of the vulnerability and arrived suddenly.
The generals and soldiers looked at each other, their faces pale,
but Shìzǔ remained composed, speaking and laughing as usual,
and his dispositions became clearer.
Thereupon, the morale of the troops was stabilized.
Tài knew there were few men inside the barricades,
and attacked fiercely day and night.
Shìzǔ inspired his generals and soldiers,
personally exposing himself to arrows and stones.
After a standoff of several tens of days,
Tài finally retreated.
When Gāozǔ sent Zhōu Wényù to lead troops to attack Kān,
Shìzǔ joined forces with him and went to Wúxīng.
At that time, Kān's army was still numerous,
occupying strategic points.
His naval and land forces formed continuous lines.
Shìzǔ ordered Generals Liú Chéng and Jiǎng Yuǎnjǔ to lead troops to attack Kān.
Kān's army suffered a great defeat,
and in desperation,
he surrendered.
Zhāng Biāo, the Inspector of Dōngyáng Prefecture, raised an army and besieged Wáng Huáizhèn, the Prefect of Línhǎi.
Huáizhèn sent an envoy to request aid.
Shìzǔ and Zhōu Wényù led light troops to Kuàijī to ambush Biāo.
Later, Biāo's general Shěn Tài opened the city gates and let Shìzǔ in.
Shìzǔ seized all of Biāo's subordinates and their families.
When Biāo arrived,
he was again defeated and fled.
The villagers of Ruòxié slew Biāo
and sent his head.

For his meritorious service, he was granted the title of Chíjié, Dūdū Kuàijī děng shí Jùn Zhūjūnsì [Commander of Military Affairs in Kuàijī and Ten Other Commanderies], Xuānyì Jiāngjūn [General Who Manifests Righteousness], and Prefect of Kuàijī.
The Yuè people in the deep mountains were all disobedient.
Shìzǔ dispatched forces to attack them,
and pacified them all.
His prestige and benevolence greatly spread.
When Gāozǔ received the abdication,
he was made Prince of Línchuān Commandery,
with an estate of two thousand households,
and was appointed Shìzhōng [Palace Attendant] and Āndōng Jiāngjūn [General Pacifying the East].
When Zhōu Wényù and Hóu Āndū were defeated at Dùnkǒu,
Gāozǔ ordered Shìzǔ to enter and guard the capital,
entrusting him with all military provisions and equipment.
Soon after, he was ordered to lead troops to fortify the southern part of Wǎn.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐngwǔ, of the third year of Yǒngdìng,
Gāozǔ passed away.
His final edict summoned Shìzǔ to assume the throne.
On the day Jiǎyín,
he arrived from Nánwǎn
and took residence in the Zhōngshūshěng.
The Empress issued an order saying:
"The Vast Heavens are unmerciful;
the High Ultimate has sent down misfortune.
The Great Departed Emperor suddenly abandoned the myriad states;
the whole land wails in sorrow,
the entire world is as if in mourning,
suffering extreme cruelty and vexation,
with no one to reach out to.
The orphans are small and helpless,
with no date for their return to the state.
A senior ruler must be established
to bring peace to the realm.
Shìzhōng, Āndōng Jiāngjūn, and Línchuān Wáng Qiàn,
is by lineage from Jǐng Huáng,
and is the only surviving nephew.
He accomplished extraordinary feats at Mùyě,
and established great achievements in conquering Lí.
At the auspicious time for entering the imperial residence,
on the day for assuming the throne and wielding power,
he equally assisted in establishing harmony,
and was part of the initial founding.
His connection to the imperial ancestral temple
is recognized by all, near and far.
It is fitting to uphold the great lineage
and succeed to the precious record,
so that the seven ancestral temples have offerings,
and the myriad people live in peace.
This survivor, clinging to her last breath,
suffers these hundred afflictions.
Meditating on this deeply,
I am overwhelmed with emotion."
Shìzǔ repeatedly declined,
even two or three times.
The multitude of dukes and high officials firmly requested him.
On that very day, he ascended the imperial throne in the Tàijí Qiándiàn.
An edict proclaimed:
"Heaven has sent down misfortune,
suddenly befalling the nation and household.
The Great Departed Emperor has left the myriad states;
the hearts of the whole land are broken,
as if mourning a deceased parent.
The imperial succession and precious calendar
have unexpectedly fallen upon Our person.
The era is fraught with turmoil,
and affairs of state are urgent.
The south-facing position requires a ruler,
and declining from the west is a minor courtesy.
Now, We shall reverently accept the auspicious mandate
and brightly govern the four seas.
A general amnesty is granted to the empire;
all crimes, regardless of severity,
are hereby purged.
Outstanding taxes and old debts,
those owed by officials and common people,
are no longer to be collected.
Civil and military officials, both within and without,
shall have their ranks proportionally increased.
Those who are filial, fraternal, diligent in farming, and succeed their fathers,
shall be granted one rank.
May all harbor reverence in their hearts,
and dukes and high officials exert their full strength,
to overcome cruelty and abolish killing,
without waiting a hundred years.
Speaking of this, Our voice chokes,
and Our grief deepens to the extreme."
Another edict commanded that all prefectures and commanderies cease their rushed travel to the capital.
In the seventh month, on the day Jǐngchén, of autumn,
the Empress was honored as Huáng Tàihòu.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Zhènnán Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ Ouyáng Wěi was promoted to Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn.
Píngnán Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī Zhōu Dí was promoted to Zhènnán Jiāngjūn.
Píngnán Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Gāozhōu Cìshǐ Huáng Fǎlì was promoted to Ānnán Jiāngjūn.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Zhènnán Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Guìzhōu Cìshǐ Chúnyú Liáng was promoted to Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Shìzhōng, Chējì Jiāngjūn, and Sīkōng Hóu Tián was made Tàiwèi.
Zhènxī Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ Hóu Āndū was made Sīkōng.
Shìzhōng, Zhōngquán Jiāngjūn, and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī Wáng Chōng was made Tèjìn, Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū.
Zhènběi Jiāngjūn and Nánsúzhōu Cìshǐ Xú Dù was made Shìzhōng, Zhōngfǔjūn Jiāngjūn, and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
On the day Rénxū,
Shìzhōng and Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Xú Shìpǔ was made Tèjìn, Ānyòu Jiāngjūn;
Shìzhōng and Zhōngwǔ Jiāngjūn Dù Léng was made Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Chóngyún Diàn suffered a fire.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Píngběi Jiāngjūn and Nánsúzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Yì was made Ānnán Jiāngjūn and Jìnzhōu Cìshǐ.
Píngnán Jiāngjūn and Běijiāngzhōu Cìshǐ Lǔ Xīdá was promoted to Ānzuǒ Jiāngjūn.
On the day Gēngxū,
Imperial Prince Bóshào was enfeoffed as Shǐxīng Wáng,
to carry on the lineage of Zhāoliè Wáng.
The heir to Shǐxīng, Xū, was transferred to be enfeoffed as Ānchéng Wáng.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Imperial Prince Bózōng was established as the Crown Prince.
Kings, dukes, and those below were granted silk, each in varying amounts.
On the day Yǐhài,
Consort Shěn was established as the Empress.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐmǎo, of winter,
Wáng Lín attacked Dàléi.
An edict was issued, dispatching Tàiwèi Hóu Tián, Sīkōng Hóu Āndū, and Yítóng Xú Dù to lead troops to resist him.
In the first month, on the day Guǐchǒu, of spring, in the first year of Tiānjiā,
an edict proclaimed:
"We, being of limited wisdom,
have succeeded to this vast enterprise.
In sorrow and mourning,
the way of governance is not yet illuminated.
Reflecting upon the former virtue,
which spread far and wide, both seen and unseen,
We respectfully hold Ourselves in silence,
hoping for no alteration.
Although grand plans and noble paths
are flourishing day by day,
the imperial ancestral temple is vast and empty,
and the sagely spirit has passed into the distant.
Thoughts of the eternal past stir,
and looking upon it, there is no end to grief.
Now the four seasons have completed their cycle,
and the three elements announce their offering.
Chinese and foreigners alike gather,
bearing jade and silk in swift homage.
We wish to extend the bequeathed beneficence,
and spread it among the myriad people.
Therefore, a great amnesty is proclaimed throughout the empire.
The fourth year of Yǒngdìng is renamed the first year of Tiānjiā.
Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves
shall be granted five *hú* of grain per person.
Those who demonstrate exceptional filial piety, fraternity, and diligence in farming
shall be granted one rank.
On the day Jiǎyín,
envoys were dispatched to comfort and inspect the four quarters.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb.
An edict proclaimed:
"We reverently offered sacrifice to the High Ultimate,
piously presenting sacrificial animals and jade.
The grand ancestral rites are completed,
sincerity and reverence both magnified.
Moreover, the lingering overcast has cleared,
and fair weather has arrived.
The clouds and elements are bright and clear,
the scenery peaceful and harmonious.
Jubilation stirs among heaven and earth,
and joy flows among the common people.
We wish to enable the populace
to share in this abundant blessing.
Therefore, the people are granted one rank."
On the day Xīnwèi,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Northern Suburb.
There was a halo around the sun.
In the second month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Old Man Star (Canopus) was seen.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Gāozhōu Cìshǐ Jì Jī rebelled from the army and returned to Xuānchéng,
holding the commandery to support Wáng Lín.
Jīng Lìng Hè Dāngqiān led troops to suppress him.
On the day Jǐngshēn,
Tàiwèi Hóu Tián defeated Wáng Lín at Liángshān,
and defeated the Qí forces at Bówàng.
He captured the Qí general Liú Bóqiú alive,
seized all their supplies, boats, and ships,
and captured tens of thousands of prisoners and severed heads.
Wáng Lín and his lord Xiāo Zhuāng fled to Qí.
On the *wùxū* day,
an edict stated:
“Indeed, the Five Phases rotate in succession,
and the Three Numinous Powers bestow their mandate.
Sovereign kings, following this, innovate and create;
this is why the Yīn and Zhōu dynasties were gladly supported.
We, inheriting the calendar and the foundation,
have greatly exalted the *Dǐng* destiny;
the principle of governance belongs to us,
and the mandate of the dynasty rests with us.
How could this be due to mere chance,
or sought through divination and prayers?
Therefore, it is known that the gravity of the divine implements
must lie in the symbols and mandates.
Hence, 'chasing the deer' invites ridicule,
disrupting settled order.
Rebellious ministers and traitorous sons,
though from different eras, share the same culpability.
Wáng Lín, with his dim insight and 'carrying a pitcher' foolishness,
his wisdom shaming even the 'guarding the feet' adage,
violated principles and disturbed norms,
bringing about his own downfall.
Yet, among the gentry and gentlemen,
many were constrained and tied.
Although the Jīng and Wèi rivers merged,
and orchids and putrid fish were sold in the same market,
when seeking the underlying reason,
some may have been coerced followers.
Now that the ‘nine-net’ has been set,
the 'eight directions' are covered.
Heaven’s net is vast and wide,
yet a fish large enough to swallow a boat can still slip through.
Just as Fúbō persuaded,
forever becoming a Hàn vassal,
and Yánshòu escaped home,
eventually becoming a Wèi guardian,
and vessels changed from Qín to Yú,
and talents were shared between Jìn and Chǔ –
whether to act or withdraw, to be employed or discarded,
is also not constant.
It is fitting to extend broad benevolence,
to manifest the 'thunderous awakening.'
Therefore, those of gentry families and scholar-officials
who were part of the wicked faction
are all hereby pardoned.
Generals and soldiers
are likewise granted a general amnesty,
and shall be appointed and promoted according to their talents,
so that their strength may be utilized.”
Another edict further stated: From the beginning of the military campaign,
those generals and soldiers who died for the state
shall all receive posthumous honors and titles.
On the *jǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
“Recently, the wicked leaders raged,
and the armies advanced to suppress them.
Ships and supplies were transported,
temporarily conscripting civilians.
The campaign has lasted for a long time,
and the labor has been arduous.
Now that the baleful influences have been cleared,
it is fitting to grant special dispensations.
The poll tax for adults is hereby remitted.
For those who were unfortunates during the conscription,
and their wives and husbands died,
their spouses and children are exempted for three years.”
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
envoys were dispatched with imperial edicts to convey the Emperor's solicitude throughout the four directions.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Grand Commandant Hóu Tiàn was sent to guard Pénchéng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Chāng, the sixth son of Gāozǔ, was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu,
and enfeoffed as King of Héngyáng.
In the third month, on the *jǐngchén* day,
an edict stated:
“Since the turmoil and chaos began,
more than ten years have passed.
The registered households have dwindled,
with hardly one in ten thousand remaining.
The common people of the Central Plains
are said to be few.
Recently, successive banditry and difficulties,
and numerous taxes and levies,
and moreover, since the army was raised,
a thousand gold pieces are spent daily.
The treasuries are depleted,
and the looms are empty year after year.
The recently provisioned military supplies
were originally for wartime readiness.
Now that the prime evil has been overcome,
and the eight directions are at peace,
weapons are sheathed,
and rest is at hand.
We desire to enable the remaining populace
to enjoy this lenient taxation.
This year's military grain tax is reduced by one-third.
The Department of State Affairs shall circulate this to the four directions,
proclaiming Our benevolent and compassionate intention.
Governors and magistrates shall diligently encourage and instruct,
prioritizing agriculture and sericulture,
so that the people, ‘drumming their bellies and holding food in their mouths,’
may return to these days.”
Sūn Yáng, the Inspector of Yǐngzhōu appointed by Xiāo Zhuāng, surrendered his entire prefecture.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Zhōu Dí, Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, pacified the Southern Central region,
beheading the bandit leader Xióng Tánlǎng,
and sending his head to the capital.
Previously,
the Qí army had guarded Lǔshān City.
On the *wùmǔ* day,
the Qí army abandoned the city and fled.
Chéng Língxǐ, Inspector of Nán Yùzhōu, was ordered to guard it.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the four commanderies of Tiānmén, Yìyáng, Nánpíng from Jīngzhōu,
and Wǔlíng from Yǐngzhōu,
were separated to establish Wǔzhōu.
Its Inspector was to oversee Yuánzhōu,
and hold the title of Administrator of Wǔlíng,
governing from Wǔlíng Commandery.
The six counties under the command of its Commandant were to form Yuánzhōu.
A separate Tōngníng Commandery was established,
with the Inspector concurrently serving as Administrator,
governing from the Commandant's city,
and the former Commandant's office was abolished.
Wú Míngchè, General for Pacifying the South, Inspector of Nányǔnzhōu, and newly appointed General of the Right Guard, was made General for Pacifying the West and Inspector of Wǔzhōu.
Sūn Yáng, the false Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, was made General for Pacifying the South and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the *jǐngzǐ* day,
King Chāng of Héngyáng passed away.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an edict stated:
“Those civil and military officials appointed by the usurper Xiāo Zhuāng who return to court
shall be evaluated and given positions.”
In the summer, fourth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Imperial Prince Bóxìn was enfeoffed as King of Héngyáng,
to continue the line of the deceased king.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Xún Lǎng, General for Pacifying the South, was made General for Pacifying the North and Inspector of Hézhōu.
In the fifth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Rǔchéng County of Guìyáng was renamed Lúyáng Commandery.
Shǐxīng and Ānyuǎn commanderies from Héngzhōu were separated
to establish Dōnghéngzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the posthumous title of Empress Jǐng’ān, Imperial Ancestress, was changed to Empress Jǐngwén.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict stated:
“Liáng Xiàoyuán suffered much hardship and difficulty,
and his spirit coffin was scattered and exiled.
We, having formerly faced north,
behaved with exceptional propriety,
sending envoys to receive it,
and moving it to a nearby route in sequence.
Since Jiāngníng is the old imperial tomb,
it is fitting to secure a burial place there immediately.
The ceremonial chariots, banners, and regulations
shall all follow the Liáng precedents,
in accordance with the precedent of Wèi burying Hàn Xiàndì.”
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the deceased Consort of Zhāoliè King of Shǐxīng was posthumously titled Consort Xiào.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Xú Dù, Minister-Supervisor with the rank of *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Army.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
for the first anniversary of the national mourning,
the Emperor presided at the Front Hall of the Tàijí Palace,
and all officials accompanied him in lamentation.
A general amnesty was granted in the capital for those sentenced to death and below.
In this month,
Emperor Yuán of Liáng was buried in Jiāngníng.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *Jiǎyín*,
an edict stated:
“I, with my humble person,
have been entrusted with the great throne,
bearing an immense burden,
and my worries and responsibilities are truly profound.
Yet, the myriad tasks are not yet settled,
and resentment still gathers.
I longingly seek the wise and worthy,
even in my dreams.
Whenever a word enters my ears,
or a fragment of goodness can be found,
how could I not praise and promote them,
binding their words to my sash?
Yet, the *Fùyán* remains empty,
the vast valleys still conceal talent.
The rush mat offerings are made in vain,
the banners and bows do not arrive.
Could it be that I have deviated from sagely governance,
leaving talent in the wilderness?
Or is the current era degenerate,
inferior to antiquity?
I often sigh while eating,
and my lamentations increase whether I am sleeping or waking.
Lù Shāncái (陸山才), the Administrator of Xīn'ān, has submitted a memorial,
recommending Xiāo Cè (蕭策), formerly the *Zhēngxī Cóngshì Zhōngláng* for the Liáng dynasty,
and Wáng Xiān (王暹), formerly the *Shàngshū Zhōngbīng Láng* for the Liáng dynasty.
Both are from prominent families, pure and illustrious,
esteemed figures in renowned clans.
Some are proficient in literature and history,
others commendable for their filial piety.
They should all be elevated to court ranks
and promoted without regard for normal procedure.
From the dukes downwards,
each should advance the worthy and virtuous,
and recommend those who are obscure and neglected.
Thus, all talents will surely gather,
and the great edifice can be built,
so that the wild trees will be praised in song,
and *Yóugēng* will be chanted.”
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
an edict stated:
“Since the recent troubles and chaos,
registered households have been displaced.
Thinking of the remaining populace,
it is truly lamentable and distressing.
For those who have lost their homes and land,
and have migrated to seek food,
this year, they shall settle wherever they wish.
Next year, regardless of whether they are new settlers or old residents,
they shall all be registered
according to the regulations for local settlement.”
On the day *Jǐngchén*, Prince Bóshān (伯山), the imperial son, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Póyáng.
In the eighth month, on the day *Gēngchén*,
the Old Man Star (Canopus) was sighted.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
an edict stated:
“Grains and pulses are more precious
than pearls and jade.
Since the recent banditry,
many have become idlers,
the common people have lost their livelihood of cultivating land,
and gentlemen are mocked for being like calves wearing sashes.
I pity the common folk
and wish to reform this corrupt custom.
I aim to prevent famine
and focus on enriching and educating the people.
Wheat is extremely vital and essential
for its uses.
Now, the ninth month is upon us,
and myriad fruits can be harvested.
Therefore, proclaim this far and wide,
and ensure that all sow seeds.
Administrators and magistrates shall personally supervise and encourage the work,
ensuring it is done in a timely manner.
For those who are extremely poor,
seeds shall be distributed according to their needs.”
On the day *Guǐwèi*,
Shìzǔ (世祖) presided over judicial proceedings at the Jǐngyáng Hall.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
an edict stated:
“The stained wine vessels and earthen drums
are indeed difficult to bring back.
But painted eggs and carved firewood
can perhaps be easily changed.
In the late era of the Liáng (梁) dynasty,
extravagance had become excessive.
Fodder and meat fed the servants,
singers and bells filled the storehouses.
Earth and wood were adorned with crimson and vermilion,
carriages and horses decorated with precious gold and jade.
The pursuit of desires flowed wildly,
and error drifted far.
I, since my student days,
was quite content with simple means.
My family upheld simplicity and frugality,
my household devoid of ostentation.
Observing the customs of the time,
I often wrung my hands in dismay.
Now, having presumptuously seized the opportune moment
to rule the realm,
and finding myself in a degenerate age,
I desire to hear of the ways of governance.
I subsist on simple food and dwell in a humble palace,
content with frugality and plainness,
so that these shallow customs
may revert to pure traditions.
Therefore, carvings and excessive ornaments,
which are not necessary for weapons or state ceremonies,
as well as gold, silver, pearls, jade,
clothing, and miscellaneous playthings,
are all hereby prohibited.”
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
Hèruò Dūn (賀若敦), a general of Zhōu (周), led one myriad cavalry and infantry
and suddenly arrived at Wǔlíng.
Wú Míngchè (吳明徹), the Inspector of Wǔzhōu, could not resist
and withdrew his army to Bālíng.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
the Emperor visited the Zhèngyáng Hall to review the troops.
In the ninth month, on the day *Guǐchǒu*,
a comet was sighted.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Dúgū Shèng (獨孤盛), a general of Zhōu, led a naval force to advance towards Bā and Xiāng,
advancing simultaneously by land and water with Hèruò Dūn (賀若敦).
Hóu Tián (侯瑱), the Grand Commandant, departed from Xúnyáng to repel them.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Xú Dù (徐度), an *Yítóng*, was dispatched to lead troops to meet Hóu Tián (侯瑱) at Bāqiū.
On the day *Jǐngzǐ*,
Venus appeared in daylight.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
an edict ordered Hóu Tián (侯瑱)'s army to advance and attack Bā and Xiāng.
In the tenth month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
Hóu Tián (侯瑱) launched a surprise attack and defeated Dúgū Shèng (獨孤盛) at Yángyè Zhōu,
capturing all his ships.
Dúgū Shèng (獨孤盛) gathered his troops and landed,
building a fortress to defend himself.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
an edict ordered Hóu Āndū (侯安都), the Minister of Works, to lead troops to join Hóu Tián (侯瑱) in the southern campaign.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Yǐwèi*,
an edict stated:
“In ancient times, during the two seasons of spring and summer,
heavy sentences were not decided.
This is because during the warmth and harmony of spring,
Heaven's order is to foster growth.
To loosen the net of punishment
is in harmony with the principle of nurturing and protecting.
This is how former kings emulated Heaven and Earth
to establish laws and impart teachings.
I, finding myself in a degenerate age,
seek to understand the people's suffering,
and my compassion and sympathy
are as deep as falling into a pit.
I have always wished to follow the old traditions
to extend civilizing influence.
From now until the beginning of summer,
for those criminals whose capital offenses have been confessed,
their executions should be temporarily suspended.”
On the day *Jǐhài*,
Yùchí Xiàn (尉遲憲), the Zhōu (周) city lord of Bālíng, surrendered.
Hóu Āndǐng (侯安鼎), the Inspector of Bāzhōu, was dispatched to guard it.
[一一]On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Dúgū Shèng (獨孤盛) secretly fled with his remaining troops from Yángyè Zhōu.
In the second year, the first month, on the day *Gēngxū*,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
Dù Léng (杜稜), General of the Cloud Banner and Administrator of Jìnlíng, was appointed as *Shìzhōng* and *Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn*.
On the day *Xīnhài*,
Prince Bómào (伯茂) of Shǐxīng was appointed as General Xuānhuì and Inspector of Yángzhōu.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Péi Jǐnghuī (裴景徽), the Inspector of Hézhōu, fled to Qí.
[一二]On the day *Xīnwèi*,
Yīn Liàng (殷亮), the Zhōu (周) city lord of Xiāngzhōu, surrendered,
and Xiāngzhōu was pacified.
In the second month, on the day *Jǐngxū*,
Hóu Tián (侯瑱), the Grand Commandant, was appointed as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
a partial amnesty was granted to the various commanderies of Xiāngzhōu.
In the third month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Hóu Tián (侯瑱), the Grand Commandant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, passed away.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
[一三]Xú Dù (徐度), General of the Pacifying East and Administrator of Kuàijī, was appointed as General of the Pacifying South and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
In the summer, fourth month,
the four commanderies of Nánpíng, Yídū, Luó, and Hédōng, from Jīngzhōu, were separated
to establish Nánjīngzhōu,
with its seat in Hédōng Commandery.
Wú Míngchè (吳明徹), General of the Pacifying West and Inspector of Wǔzhōu, was appointed as Inspector of Nánjīngzhōu.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
Lǔ Xīdá (魯悉達), General of the Pacifying Left, was appointed as General of the Pacifying South and Inspector of Wúzhōu.
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,
the Old Man Star (Canopus) was sighted.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *Jǐngwǔ*,
Hèruò Dūn (賀若敦), a Zhōu (周) general, withdrew and retreated on his own,
with seventeen or eighteen out of ten (70-80%) of his men and animals perishing.
Wǔlíng, Tiānmén, Nánpíng, Yìyáng, Hédōng, and Yídū commanderies were all pacified.
In the ninth month, on the *Jiǎyín* day,
an edict stated:
“The enterprise of the Jī [Dynasty] was just beginning to flourish,
its aspirations borne on the bank of the Wèi River.
The Hàn’s mandate was already consolidated,
its way reaching the top of the crumbling wall.
When the essence of the stars and constellations is spread,
and the spirits descend onto the lofty peaks,
and wind and clouds are roused,
and sought in dreams,
this is indeed like a boat and salted plums,
each serving as a reciprocal sign,
for establishing nations for a long age,
and there is none that is not so.
As for inscribing virtues in the Tàicháng Temple [of ancestral worship]
and being worshipped in the Qīngmiào Temple,
to pass on to one's descendants
and to be preserved eternally.
The former emperor managed the realm,
and created all things.
Auspicious blessings were distinctly manifested,
and he gloriously received the precious mandate.
Although his sagely enlightenment was profound and manifest,
and the seen and unseen realms collectively followed,
it was also due to the virtuous and capable civil and military officials
who assisted in spreading the royal enterprise.
Therefore, the former Grand Marshal (*Dàsīmǎ*), General of Agile Cavalry (*Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn*), Tián;
the former Minister of Works (*Sīkōng*), Wényù;
the former General Who Pacifies the North (*Píngběi Jiāngjūn*), Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers (*Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*), Sēngmíng;
the former Central Protector of the Army (*Zhōnghùjūn*), Yǐng;
and the former General of the Palace Army (*Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn*), Nǐ;
some established the foundation amidst hardship,
and managed affairs through ease and peril;
some broke through enemy lines and braved blades,
sacrificing their lives for righteousness;
some widely propagated wisdom and coordinated strategies,
meticulously planning in the war tent;
some cleared thickets and toiled with horses,
diligent and hardworking from beginning to end;
all wholeheartedly devoted their efforts,
in both times of prosperity and adversity.
I, being of limited intelligence,
have succeeded to the great inheritance.
Reflecting on their illustrious achievements,
I intend to promote the canonical teachings.
It is therefore permissible to follow the old precedents
and widely praise their magnificent conduct.
They shall all be granted co-worship in the temple of Gāozǔ,
so that this great principle
may be eternally passed down in the ancestral temple.”
On the *Jǐngchén* day,

Wáng Chōng, who held the titles of Palace Attendant (*Shìzhōng*), General of the Central Authority (*Zhōngquán Jiāngjūn*), Special Advance (*Tèjìn*), Grand Master of the Left Glorious Happiness (*Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū*), and Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers (*Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*), was appointed Administrator of Dānyáng (*Dānyáng Yǐn*).
Shěn Jūnlǐ, Administrator of Dānyáng, was appointed Minister of the Left for the People (*Zuǒ Mín Shàngshū*),
and concurrently Palace Colonel of Infantry (*Bùbīng Xiàowèi*).
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the *Yǐsì* day,
〔一四〕the Man barbarians of the Western Mountains of Huòzhōu led their tribes to submit.
In the eleventh month, on the *Yǐmǎo* day,
the kingdom of Gāojùlǐ sent envoys to offer local products.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
Wǔchāng and Guóchuan were established as Jìnglín Commandery,
to settle the displaced people.
In the twelfth month, on the *Xīnsì* day,
Sūn Yáng, General Who Pacifies the East (*Āndōng Jiāngjūn*) and Grand Administrator of Wújùn, was appointed Central Protector of the Army (*Zhōnghùjūn*).
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
the temple of the kingdom of Shǐxīng was established in the capital,
using the rites appropriate for a king.
Yú Lì, Crown Prince's Middle Palace Attendant (*Tàizǐ Zhōngshùzǐ*), and Kǒng Huàn, Censor-in-Chief (*Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng*), believing that state funds were insufficient,
proposed the establishment of a salt tax and a monopoly on alcohol.
An edict ordered both to be implemented.
Previously,
Liú Yì, Inspector of Jìnzhōu, had rebelled in concert with Wáng Lín and others.
On the *Jǐngxū* day,
an edict ordered Hóu Āndū, Minister of Works, to lead troops to suppress him.
In the third year, in the spring, in the first month, on the *Gēngxū* day,
a canopy palace was set up in the southern suburbs,
and offerings were made to Hú Gōng to be co-worshipped with Heaven.
On the *Xīnhài* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice in the southern suburbs.
An edict stated:
“I bear the precious mandate,
and frequently adjust the celestial mechanisms.
Apprehensive and diligent,
I hope for stability and order.
However, moral transformation has not been accepted,
and societal ills are worsening.
Reflecting on this,
I cannot forget it day or night.
The benevolent *yáng* energy spreads its warmth,
manifestly serving the Supreme Heaven.
Personally offering the sacrificial animals and jade,
my sincerity combines with reverence for the worship.
I wish for the common people to receive this leniency and grace.
Therefore, a universal grant of one rank of nobility shall be bestowed upon the people.
For those filial and fraternal, and diligent in agriculture,
an additional rank shall be granted.”
On the *Xīnyǒu* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice in the northern suburbs.
In the intercalary second month, on the *Jǐyǒu* day,
Yú Míng, King of Bǎijì, was appointed Grand General Who Comforts the East (*Fǔdōng Dàjiāngjūn*).
Gāo Tāng, King of Gāojùlǐ, was appointed General Who Pacifies the East (*Níngdōng Jiāngjūn*).
Zhōu Dí, Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, raised troops in response to Liú Yì,
attacked Pénchéng,
and assaulted Yùzhāng Commandery,
but neither was successful.
On the *Xīnhài* day,
Wú Míngchè, Inspector of Nánjīngzhōu, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Right (*Ānyòu Jiāngjūn*).
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
the *wǔzhū* coins were recast.
In the third month, on the *Jǐngzǐ* day,
Ānchéng Wáng Xū arrived from Zhōu.
An edict appointed him Palace Attendant (*Shìzhōng*), Director of the Central Secretariat (*Zhōngshū Jiān*), and General of the Central Guards (*Zhōngwèi Jiāngjūn*),
and ordered the establishment of assistant officials for him.
On the *Dīngchǒu* day,
Wú Míngchè, General Who Pacifies the Right, was appointed General Who Pacifies the South (*Ānnán Jiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu,
and was ordered to oversee the southern expedition of the various armies.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
Hóu Āndū, Minister of Works, defeated Liú Yì at Táozhī Lǐng.
〔一五〕Yì escaped and fled to Jìn’ān,
and Dōngyáng Commandery was pacified.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the *Guǐmǎo* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Dōngyáng Commandery.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Qí sent envoys to pay respects.
In the sixth month, on the *Jǐngchén* day,
Ānchéng Wáng Xū, who held the titles of Palace Attendant, General of the Central Guards, and Inspector of Yángzhōu, was appointed General of Agile Cavalry (*Piàojì Jiāngjūn*).
The eight commanderies of Huìjī, Dōngyáng, Línhǎi, Yǒngjiā, Xīn’ān, Xīnníng, Jìn’ān, and Jiàn’ān were established as Dōngyángzhōu.
Bó Mào, Prince of Shǐxīng and Inspector of Yángzhōu, was appointed General Who Guards the East (*Zhèndōng Jiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Dōngyángzhōu.

Hóu Āndū, General Who Attacks the North (*Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn*), Minister of Works, and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, was appointed Palace Attendant and Grand General Who Attacks the North (*Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn*).
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the *Jǐchǒu* day,
the Crown Prince married Consort Wáng.
All civil and military officials in office were granted silk, with varying amounts.
Those who were filial and fraternal, diligent in agriculture, and became their fathers' successors were granted two ranks of nobility.
In the ninth month, on the first day, *Wùchén*,
there was a solar eclipse.

Dào Zhòngjǔ, who held the titles of Palace Attendant and Minister of the Department of State Affairs (*Dūguān Shàngshū*), was appointed Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs (*Shàngshū Yòu Púyè*) and Administrator of Dānyáng.
On the *Dīnghài* day,
Zhōu Dí requested to surrender.
An edict ordered Ānchéng Wáng Xū to oversee the armies to recruit and pacify him.
In this year,
Xiāo Chá, the King of Liáng established by Zhōu, died.
His son, Kuí, succeeded him.
In the fourth year, in the spring, in the first month, on the *Jǐngzǐ* day,
the kingdom of Gānlì sent envoys to offer local products.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
Zhōu Dí abandoned the city and fled.
Chén Bǎo Yìng, Inspector of Mínzhōu, took him in,
and Línchuān Commandery was pacified.
On the *Rénchén* day,
Zhāng Zhāodá, General Who Pacifies the West (*Píngxī Jiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, was appointed Protector-General (*Hùjūn Jiāngjūn*).
Huá Jiǎo, General of Resolute Martiality (*Rénwǔ Jiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Xīnzhōu, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South (*Píngnán Jiāngjūn*).

Huáng Fǎlì, General Who Guards the South (*Zhènnán Jiāngjūn*), Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers, and Inspector of Gāozhōu, was appointed Grand General Who Guards the North (*Zhènběi Dàjiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu.
Zhōu Fū, General Who Pacifies the West (*Ānxī Jiāngjūn*) and concurrently Grand Administrator of Línchuān, was appointed Inspector of Nányùzhōu.
Sūn Yáng, Central Protector of the Army, was appointed General Who Guards the Right (*Zhènyòu Jiāngjūn*).
Gāozhōu was abolished and merged into Jiāngzhōu.
In the second month, on the *Wùxū* day,

Ōuyáng Wèi, General Who Attacks the South (*Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn*), Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers, and Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, was promoted to Grand General Who Attacks the South (*Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn*).
On the *Gēngxū* day,
Hóu Āndū, who held the titles of Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Grand General Who Attacks the North, was appointed Grand General Who Attacks the South and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
Huá Jiǎo, General Who Pacifies the South, was appointed Inspector of Nánxiāngzhōu.
〔一六〕
In the third month, on the *Xīnwèi* day,

Xú Dù, General Who Guards the South and Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers, was appointed Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Central Army (*Zhōngjūn Dàjiāngjūn*).
On the *Xīnsì* day,
an edict granted posthumous honors to the officers and soldiers who died for the state while suppressing Zhōu Dí.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the *Xīnchǒu* day,
a grand Wújī assembly was held in the Tàijí Front Hall.
On the *Yǐmǎo* day,

Ānchéng Wáng Xū, who held the titles of Palace Attendant, Director of the Central Secretariat, General of the Central Guards, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Yángzhōu, was appointed Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers.
In the fifth month, on the *Dīngmǎo* day,
Xú Shìpǔ, General Who Secures the Front (*Ānqián Jiāngjūn*) and Grand Master of the Right Glorious Happiness, died.
In the sixth month, on the *Guǐsì* day,
the planet Venus was seen during the day.
Hóu Āndū, Minister of Works, was granted death.
In the seventh month, on the *Dīngchǒu* day,

Huáng Fǎlì, Grand General Who Guards the North, Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers, and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, was appointed Grand General Who Guards the South (*Zhènnán Dàjiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the *Rénxū* day,
Ōuyáng Wèi, Grand Administrator with the same authority as the Three Ducal Ministers and Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, passed away.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to the capital.
On the *Xīnwèi* day,
Zhōu Dí again raided Línchuān.
An edict ordered Zhāng Zhāodá, Protector-General, to lead troops to suppress him.
In the eleventh month, on the *Xīnyǒu* day,
Zhāng Zhāodá greatly defeated Zhōu Dí,
capturing all his partisans.
Dí escaped and went into hiding.
In the twelfth month, on the *Jǐngshēn* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
An edict ordered Zhāng Zhāodá, Protector-General, to advance to Jiàn’ān,
to suppress Chén Bǎo Yìng.
Yú Xiàqǐn, General Who Inspires Awe (*Xìnwēi Jiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Yìzhōu, was ordered to lead the armies from Huìjī, Dōngyáng, Línhǎi, and Yǒngjiā, to meet him from the eastern route.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
Wú Míngchè, former General Who Secures the South (*Ānnán Jiāngjūn*) and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed General Who Guards the Front (*Zhènqián Jiāngjūn*).
In the fifth year, in spring, the first month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Yuán Shū, Minister of Personnel and General-in-Chief of the Right Army, was appointed Administrator of Dānyáng Commandery.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the northern suburbs.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
a fire broke out in Péngchéng, Jiāngzhōu,
killing over two hundred people.
In the third month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Chún'yú Liàng, General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South, Administrator with the Rank of *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, and Governor of Guìzhōu, was appointed Grand General of the Central Pacifying Army.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an edict ordered Zhōu Tiěhǔ, the late Protection Army General, to be offered sacrifices in the ancestral temple of Gāozǔ.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zhōu sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Nándānyáng Commandery was abolished.
In this month,
Zhōu and Qí both sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
at night,
there were two streaks of white vapor,
emerging from the southeast of the Big Dipper,
reaching the ground.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, with my limited understanding,
am burdened with this heavy responsibility.
The seasons frequently change,
and the imperial crown is never vacant.
I have been unable to align myself with the celestial spheres,
to bring harmony to the world,
to comfort the common people,
and to bring peace to the multitudes.
Wars are incessant,
and the people lack years of plenty.
The way of transforming customs has not been widely spread,
and the harm of old habits still persists.
This has caused many commoners to fall into the net of the law,
and officials to frequently amend records.
Prisons have become increasingly crowded.
Although this is due to people's offenses,
and those in prison are long detained,
there may also be injustices.
Remembering my vow to save those in distress,
I have toiled behind the screen.
Furthermore, my health has not been well,
and my care has been lacking.
Having recently recovered slightly,
I wish to extend broad clemency.
Therefore, a partial amnesty for the capital is granted."
In the ninth month,
the Western City was fortified.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Chéng Língxǐ, General of the Left Guard, was appointed Protection Army General.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Zhāodá defeated Chén Bǎo'yìng in Jiàn'ān,
captured Bǎo'yìng and Liú Yì,
sent them to the capital,
and Jiàn'ān Commandery was pacified.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zhāng Zhāodá, Protection Army General, was appointed General Who Guards the Front and Administrator with the Rank of *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to the two commanderies of Jiàn'ān and Jìn'ān.
For the officers and soldiers who died for the state in the campaign against Chén Bǎo'yìng,
coffins were provided,
and their bodies were sent back to their hometowns,
and their families were granted immunity from corvée.
Those with unhealed wounds
were provided with medical treatment.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Qí sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the sixth year, in spring, the first month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Crown Prince reached adulthood (was capped).
Kings, dukes, and officials below them were granted silk according to their ranks.
Those who were filial, fraternal, and diligent in farming, and succeeded their fathers, were granted one rank of nobility.
Widowers, widows, orphans, and the lonely who could not support themselves were given five *hú* of grain per person.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Dù Léng, General of the Supervising Army, was appointed General Who Guards the Left Flank and Administrator of Dānyáng Commandery.
Yuán Shū, Administrator of Dānyáng Commandery, was appointed Minister of Personnel.
Shěn Qīn, Minister of the Imperial Guard, was appointed General of the Central Supervising Army.
In the third month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict ordered that those who, since Hóu Jǐng's rebellion, had been displaced and moved to Jiàn'ān, Jìn'ān, and Yì'ān Commanderies,
were all allowed to return to their native lands.
Those who had been captured and made slaves
were to be freed as commoners.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,

Ānchéng Wáng Xū, Attendant-in-ordinary, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, General of the Central Guard, General of Agile Cavalry, Administrator with the Rank of *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, and Governor of Yángzhōu, was appointed Minister of Works.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
a comet was seen.
[一七]Zhōu sent envoys to offer tribute.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
a strong wind came from the southwest,
more than a hundred paces wide,
destroying the observatory tower of the Spirit Terrace.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Yíxiántáng Hall collapsed without cause.
On the *jǐngxū* day,
Luò Wényá, Administrator of Línchuān, beheaded Zhōu Dí,
[一八]sent his head to the capital,
and displayed it on the Zhūquè Bridge.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Venus was seen during the day.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Liáng dynasty has faced many misfortunes,
with disasters following one after another.
Weapons have clashed incessantly,
unresolved for ten years.
The unruly elements cruelly abused the living,
and the lawless rabble even harmed the spirits of the deceased.
When the state was first established on the east of the Jiāng River,
it was a residence for kings.
Lords of the Metal and Water elements,
and rulers of the Wood and Fire virtues,
the era has changed through four dynasties,
exceeding two hundred years.
As for those who managed the imperial [一九]enterprise,
the gentry, and the hopes of the people,
loyal ministers and filial sons,
there was no age without talent,
[二０]yet they lie scattered on hills,
and the landscapes of the mountains and valleys have changed.
Some were all cut down,
none were spared from harm.
Jade cups were found among the people,
and lacquer slips were passed down through generations.
No longer are there five-tree groves,
and ancient markers are rarely seen.
Since the great reign began to shine,
we respectfully observed the tradition of abdication.
Now, as I, myself, am on the throne,
I follow the path of my ancestors.
Although our flags and colors,
still follow the customs of the Guì and Sòng [二一]states,
whenever the imperial carriage tours,
I look longingly towards the roads of the Hé and Luò rivers.
Thus, the sacrifices at Qiáoshān
are not lacking in offerings,
and the tombs at Líshān
are constantly guarded by pines and cypresses.
However, the old mounds of imperial relatives and vassals,
and the former tombs of scholars,
are not yet fully covered,
and firewood gathering and pasturing are still common.
Some relatives are dispersed and enslaved,
with no date to return to bury their dead.
Descendants are extinct,
to whom can the planted trees be entrusted?
Emperor Gāo lingered over Wú Jì,
and Emperor Sòng Gāozǔ sighed over Zǐfáng.
Sorrow arises from graves,
a feeling shared by all human souls.
[二二]Therefore, I speak these words for a long time,
thinking to comfort those in the netherworld.
As for the former kings and marquises,
and the loyal and valiant ones of ancient times,
whose tombs have been disturbed and who have no descendants,
let them be inspected and repaired.
Trees in the tombs
must not be cut for firewood.
May the seen and unseen realms all flourish,
in accordance with my wishes."
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the imperial prince Bó Gù was enthroned as Prince of Xīn'ān Commandery.
Bó Gōng was enthroned as Prince of Jìn'ān.
Bó Rén was enthroned as Prince of Lúlíng.
Bó Yì was enthroned as Prince of Jiāngxià.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Yùzhāng Commandery was abolished.
In this month,
a new large bridge was built.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Qí sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Imperial Prince Bólǐ 伯禮 was established as the Prince of Wǔlíng 武陵.
On the day Dīngsì,
Zhāng Zhāodá 章昭達, General of the Vanguard and Kōngfǔ Yítóng Sānsī 開府儀同三司, was appointed General of the South and Governor of Jiāngzhōu 江州.
Huáng Fǎfù 黃法氋, Grand General of the South and Governor of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed Grand General of the Central Guard.
Chéng Língxǐ 程靈洗, Central Protector-General, was appointed General of Strategic Might and Governor of Yǐngzhōu 郢州.
Shěn Kè 沈恪, General of the Army and Governor of Yǐngzhōu, was appointed Central Protector-General.
Wú Míngchè 吳明徹, General of the East and Administrator of Wúxīng 吳興, was appointed Central Leader of the Army.
On the day Wǔwǔ,
Prince Bóshān 伯山 of Póyáng 鄱陽, East Central Commander and Administrator of Wújùn 吳郡, was appointed General Pacifying the North and Governor of Nánxúzhōu 南徐州.
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict stated:
"Since I have occupied the important position of governing the people,
and have been placed above kings and dukes,
I reflect on my foolishness
and feel vexed by the way of governance.
Furthermore, I have frequently failed in listening and observing,
so matters have accumulated and become stagnant,
with grievances and detentions unredressed,
and hidden injustices unexamined.
Thinking of these criminals,
it is worse than falling into a pit.
Yet, benevolent favor has not flowed,
and the dry season has lasted for months.
Now, as the year draws to a close,
and the New Year approaches,
I wish that those within the dark prisons
may equally receive the blessings of the season.
Therefore, a partial amnesty is granted to the capital."
In the first year of Tiānkāng 天康, spring, second month, on the day Jǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, with my meager virtue,
have inherited the great lineage.
From dawn to dusk, I have toiled,
hoping to expand this glorious enterprise.
Yet, the path of governance is often obscure,
and the common people are not yet at peace.
Moreover, illness has lingered,
and drought has persisted for months.
What fault do the hundred surnames have?
Indeed, the fault lies with me.
Thinking of this constantly,
it pains me as if I had a sick head.
Therefore, a general amnesty is granted to all under Heaven,
and the seventh year of Tiānjiā 天嘉 is changed to the first year of Tiānkāng."
In the third month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Xiū 頊, Prince of Ānchéng 安成, General of Agile Cavalry, Kōngfǔ Yítóng Sānsī, Governor of Yángzhōu 揚州, and newly appointed Minister of the Palace, was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Imperial Grandson Zhìzé 至澤 was born.
All civil and military officials in office were granted varying amounts of silk,
and those who succeeded their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Shìzǔ's 世祖 illness became severe.
On this day,
he passed away in the Yǒujué Diàn 有覺殿.
His dying edict stated:
"My illness has lingered,
and now it has reached the point of no recovery.
Life's span is fated;
what more can be said?
But the imperial enterprise has been difficult,
with military campaigns for successive years,
and the common people have suffered greatly;
I can never forget my shame and apprehension.
Now the four corners are settled,
but the popular teachings have not yet spread widely.
To reach this great decline now
is a lasting regret.
The responsibility for the state is heavy;
the Crown Prince may immediately ascend the throne.
Kings, marquises, generals, and ministers,
assist him well.
Let internal and external affairs be harmonious;
do not go against my will!
The imperial tomb should be kept simple and completed quickly.
After the grand enshrouding,
all officials shall pay respects once every three days.
The system of public mourning
shall generally follow the old regulations."
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the officials conferred the posthumous title Emperor Wén 文 and
the temple name Shìzǔ.
On the day Jǐngyín,
he was buried in Yǒngníng Líng 永寧陵.
Shìzǔ rose from difficult circumstances
and understood the suffering of the common people.
For state expenditures,
he always practiced frugality.
Whenever taxes and levies were unavoidable,
he would sigh and change his expression,
as if the burden were on himself.
When officials presented matters for decision,
he subtly discerned truth from falsehood,
allowing no treachery from below,
so people knew to exert themselves.
Throughout the night, those who entered the inner chambers to take external documents for judgment
came one after another.
Whenever the palace servants observed the water clock
and passed the changing watch-tablet within the hall,
he would command the bearers to throw the tablet onto the stone steps,
making a clanging sound,
saying,
"Even if I am asleep,
this will startle me awake."
Such instances of his overall conduct,
from beginning to end, were many.
Yáo Chá 姚察, Minister of Personnel for Chén 陳, said: "The world praises those who inherit and preserve the legacy,
and those of the imperial branch who continue the tradition.
The distinction between success and failure
is quite clear.
Generally, to uphold and not let fall is considered virtuous and capable,
while to bend and change is considered unworthy.
Those who can glorify the former path
and successfully bear the burden of their ancestors' achievements
are indeed few.
From his initial rise, Shìzǔ's
achievements and merits were prominent.
He pacified chaos and quelled bandits,
first assisting in the great enterprise.
When national calamity suddenly arrived,
he entered to inherit the throne,
acting with such trepidation
as if driving a decaying chariot.
[(Page 23)] Moreover, he esteemed Confucian arts
and delighted in literary works.
He saw goodness as if he could not attain it,
and employed people as if they were his own.
He governed himself with reverence and frugality,
and helped the people with diligence.
From ancient times, such truly civil and truly martial rulers,
after whom the East longed and the West complained,
their true deeds
can be compared to his.
As for relying on intelligence
and using discernment,
this was the governance of Yǒngpíng 永平;
the former historians shall discuss it.
In the third year of Tiānjiā,
King Gāo Tāng 高湯 of Gāogōulí 高句驪,
or in some versions,
'Gāo Yáng' 高陽.
Correction note:
Annals 4: The Deposed Emperor.
The Deposed Emperor's personal name was Bózōng 伯宗,
courtesy name Fèngyè 奉業,
childhood name Yàowáng 藥王.
He was Shìzǔ's eldest legitimate son.
He was born in the third year of Liáng Chéngshèng 梁承聖, fifth month, on the day Gēngyín.
In the second year of Yǒngdìng 永定, second month, on the day Wùchén,
he was appointed Crown Prince of Línchuān Wáng 臨川王.
In the third year,
Shìzǔ ascended the throne,
and in the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
he was established as Imperial Crown Prince.
Since the chaos and destruction of the Liáng 梁 dynasty,
the Eastern Palace had been burned.
The Crown Prince resided in Yǒngfú Shěng 永福省.
In the first year of Tiānkāng, fourth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Shìzǔ passed away.
On that same day,
the Crown Prince ascended the imperial throne in the Tàijí Qiándiàn 太極前殿.
An imperial edict stated:
"Heaven has sent down calamity;
the late Emperor suddenly abandoned the myriad states.
My cries of grief are in vain,
my inner being is shattered.
I, with my meager virtue,
have inherited the precious mandate.
Alone in my sorrow,
my fear is as great as a dangling banner.
I now rely on the prime ministers to rectify my shortcomings.
A general amnesty is granted to all under Heaven."
Another edict commanded all civil and military officials, both inside and outside the capital,
to each resume their duties,
and those from distant regions were all to cease rushing to the capital.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐmǎo (乙),
the Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager,
and the Empress as Empress Dowager.
On the day Gēngyín,
Xiū, Prince of Ānchéng, General of Agile Cavalry, Sīkōng 司空, Governor of Yángzhōu, and newly appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
His rank was advanced to Sītú 司徒, Administrator of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Commander of All Military Affairs, Internal and External.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Xú Dù 徐度, Grand General of the Central Army and Kōngfǔ Yítóng Sānsī, was advanced to the rank of Sīkōng.
Zhāng Zhāodá, General of the South, Kōngfǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Governor of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed Grand Councilor and
his title advanced to General Who Conquers the South.
Bómào 伯茂, Prince of Shǐxīng 始興, General of the East and Governor of Dōngyángzhōu 東揚州, was advanced to the title General Who Conquers the East and Kōngfǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
Bóshān, Prince of Póyáng, General Pacifying the North and Governor of Nánxúzhōu, was advanced to the title General Protecting the North.
Yuán Shū 袁樞, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Left Palace Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat.
Shěn Qīn 沈欽, General of Cloud-like Banners and Administrator of Wúxīng, was appointed Right Palace Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat.
Wú Míngchè, newly appointed Central Leader of the Army, was appointed Leader of the Army.
Shěn Kè, newly appointed Central Protector-General, was appointed Protector-General.
Huá Jiǎo 華皎, General Pacifying the South and Governor of Xiāngzhōu 湘州, was advanced to the title General Pacifying the South.
Xú Líng 徐陵, Mounted Regular Attendant and Palace Assistant Censor, was appointed Minister of Personnel.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Wáng Tōng 王通, General Assisting the Right and Grand Master of the Right for Glorious Happiness, was advanced to the title General Pacifying the Right.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Consort Wáng 王氏 was established as Empress.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the imperial carriage proceeded to offer sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Zhōu (Northern Zhōu) sent envoys to offer condolences.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the kingdom of Gāolí (Goguryeo) sent envoys to present local products.
In the spring of the first month of Guāngdà元年 (567 CE), on the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Left Prime Minister of the Department of State Affairs, Yuán Shū, passed away.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, August Heaven established its mandate,
and the precious diagram descended.
Two sovereigns shone brightly,
and the nine regions were all well-governed.
I am weak and shallow,
and the Kingly Way has not yet become manifest.
I bear this divine artifact
as if traversing a perilous sea.
I hope that worthy relatives and virtuous officials will be established in parallel,
and the regional governors will be excellent,
so that the empire may be harmonious and prosperous,
and remotely achieve a state where punishments are unused.
Now the three cycles have changed their calendar,
and myriad nations fill the court.
The pure ancestral temple has no successor,
but the assembled officials are present.
I gaze upon the vacant throne,
and my heart is shattered with grief.
I wish to spread the late emperor's beneficence
to all the people.
Therefore, a general amnesty is proclaimed throughout the empire.
Tiānkāng二年 is changed to Guāngdà元年.
Those who are filial, fraternal, and diligent in agriculture shall be granted one rank of nobility."
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Wú Míngchè, the General of the Imperial Guards, was appointed Governor of Dānyáng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Yú Xiàoqǐng, the General who Declared Martial Might and Governor of Nányùzhōu, was executed for plotting rebellion.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Xiǎo Bómào, the Prince of Shǐxīng, General who Pacified the East, Minister with Special Privileges, and Governor of Dōngyángzhōu, was appointed Grand General of the Central Guards.
Huáng Fǎchǔ, Minister with Special Privileges, was appointed General who Guarded the North and Governor of Nánsúzhōu.
Xiǎo Bóshān, the Prince of Póyáng, General who Guarded the North, and Governor of Nánsúzhōu, was appointed General who Pacified the East and Governor of Dōngyángzhōu.
In the third month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Shěn Qīn, the Right Prime Minister of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Palace Attendant and Left Prime Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Wú Míngchè, the General of the Imperial Guards and Governor of Dānyáng, was appointed General who Pacified the South and Governor of Xiāngzhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Dù Léng, the General who Guarded the Right, was appointed General of the Imperial Guards.
Huá Jiǎo, the General who Pacified the South and Governor of Xiāngzhōu, plotted rebellion.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Chúnyú Liàng, the Grand General of the Central Pacification, was appointed Imperial Commissioner, Grand General who Conquered the South,
to lead the navy in suppressing him.
In the sixth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Xú Dù, the Grand General of the Central Army and Minister of Works, was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry,
and made overall commander of the various armies of the capital region,
to advance by land and attack Xiāngzhōu.
In the intercalary month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Xiǎo Bógù, the Prince of Xīn'ān and General of Cloud Banners, was appointed Governor of Dānyáng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Imperial Prince Zhìzé was established as Crown Prince.
Those throughout the empire who were heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
Princes, dukes, ministers, and gentlemen below were bestowed silk according to their respective ranks.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The rebel Huá Jiǎo,
of extreme wickedness and depravity,
has gone so far as to enthrone Xiāo Kuí,
plotting to endanger the state.
Abandoning kin for enemies,
he has incurred the wrath of both men and gods.
Our royal army advances like lightning,
both by water and land pressing forward.
The time for his execution
is not far off.
His family members residing in the Běilǐ Shàngfāng,
shall be put to death,
to make clear the national law."
On the *gēngchén* day,
the kingdom of Báijì (Baekje) sent envoys to present local products.
In this month,
Tuòbá Dìng, the Duke of Chánghú and general of Zhōu, led 20,000 infantry and cavalry into Yǐngzhōu,
and advanced concurrently with Huá Jiǎo by water and land.
Commander-in-chief Chúnyú Liàng, Wú Míngchè, and others engaged them in battle,
and utterly routed them.
Jiǎo fled alone in a skiff to Jiānglíng.
Tuòbá Dìng was captured,
over ten thousand men were taken captive,
and over four thousand horses were seized.
They were sent to the capital.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
an amnesty was granted to those in Xiāng and Bā (counties) [zhōu] who had been misled by Jiǎo.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Shěn Kè, the General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed General who Pacified the West and Governor of Jīngzhōu.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wáng Chōng, Palace Attendant, General of the Central Army of the Right, Minister with Special Privileges, Special Appointee, and Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left, passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Kǒng Yīngzhé, concurrently Assistant Palace Attendant, was appointed Marquis of Fèngshèng Tíng,
to oversee the sacrifices to Confucius.
In the spring of the first month of the second year (568 CE), on the *jǐhài* day,

Xiāo Xù, the Prince of Ānchéng, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-chief of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Capital, Grand General of Cavalry, Minister of Education, and Supervisor of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Yángzhōu, was promoted to Grand Tutor,
retaining the post of Minister of Education,
granted exceptional honors,
permitted to wear a sword and shoes into the palace hall.
Zhāng Zhāodá, Palace Attendant, General who Conquered the South, Minister with Special Privileges, and Governor of Jiāngzhōu, was promoted to Grand General who Conquered the South.

Chúnyú Liàng, Grand General of Central Pacification and newly appointed Grand General who Conquered the South, was appointed Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Central Army, and Minister with Special Privileges.
Wú Míngchè, General who Pacified the South and Governor of Xiāngzhōu, retained his current title and was appointed Minister with Special Privileges,
and promoted to General who Guarded the South.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered that all soldiers who died in the campaign against Huá Jiǎo be provided with coffins,
returned to their native places,
and their families exempted from service.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wúzhōu was abolished,
and Póyáng Commandery was returned to Jiāngzhōu.
Xú Dù, Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and General of Chariots and Cavalry, passed away.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Jìn'ān Commandery of Dōngyángzhōu was detached to form Fēngzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Xiāo Xù, the Prince of Ānchéng and Grand Tutor, presented a jade seal.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
a comet was observed.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the kingdom of Xīnluó (Silla) sent envoys to present local products.
On the *rénxū* day,
Imperial Prince Bózhì was established as the Prince of Yǒngyáng,
and Bómóu as the Prince of Guìyáng.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
the kingdom of Línyì (Champa) sent envoys to present local products.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the kingdom of Lángyáxiū (Langkasuka) sent envoys to present local products.
Zhāng Zhāodá, Palace Attendant, Grand General who Conquered the South, Minister with Special Privileges, and Governor of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed Grand General of Central Pacification.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Shěn Kè, the former General who Pacified the West and Governor of Jīngzhōu, was appointed General of the Imperial Guard.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Huáng Fǎchǔ, General who Guarded the North, Minister with Special Privileges, and Governor of Nánsúzhōu, was appointed General who Guarded the West and Governor of Yǐngzhōu.
Chúnyú Liàng, the newly appointed Grand General of the Central Army and Minister with Special Privileges, was appointed General who Guarded the North and Governor of Nánsúzhōu.
On the *jiǎyín* day,

Empress Dowager Cíxùn assembled the assembled officials in the court hall and issued an order: "Grand General of the Central Army and Minister with Special Privileges, General who Guarded the North and Minister with Special Privileges, General who Guarded the Right, General of the Imperial Guard, and the Eight Ministers: In the late period of the Liáng dynasty's fortunes,
and the common people of the world
were almost completely wiped out.
Emperor Gāozǔ Wǔdǐ rectified the chaos and restored order,
receiving the divine mandate and imperial records.
He once again hung the three luminaries
and restored the two primary forces.
Emperor Shìzǔ Wén
Dì inherited the grand foundation,
and greatly proclaimed the precious enterprise,
benefitting and nurturing the central plains,
and pacifying the outer wilds.
Both were extremely cautious and diligent,
toiling to establish the state,
hoping that the dynasty's fortunes
would
flourish like those of the Yīn and Xià.
Bó Zōng, while in the Eastern Palace (as Crown Prince),
originally had no good reputation.
Upon reaching the highest position,
he indulged in cruelty and debauchery.
During the mourning period,
he was indeed not sorrowful or grieved.
He did not separate from his concubines,
and
successive visits to their residences continued.
It was not merely that the garments and carriages he accepted
were criticized by the Zōngzhèng,
but that giving birth to children during the mourning period
earned the scorn of the Yòushī.
What could the seven hundred years of fortune depend on?
The three thousand crimes
were great.
Moreover, he lavishly drew upon gold and silk,
to fill the imperial women's quarters.
The inner palace treasury,
military supplies, and national reserves
were, in less than a year,
all depleted.
The Grand Tutor personally received
the dying entrustment,
to guard the palace.
The late emperor's testament was earnest,
and the duty to protect the imperial household was profound.
However, before the funeral carriage was even used,
and before the day was past,
he dispatched Liú Shīzhī, Yīn Bùnìng, and others
openly rejected.
Hán Zǐgāo was a petty, frivolous servant,
yet was entrusted with heartfelt reliance.
(He engaged in) treacherous plots and caused chaos,
which erupted from within the imperial court.
Although Yuán Xiàng maintained order,
he only removed those at the ruler's side.
Furthermore, as Yú Xiàogǐng was close to the capital,
he was summoned.
The fault for the calamities and wickedness
lay with the villains who were captured.
The spirits of the ancestral temples and altars of state
eliminated the demonic miasma.
Thereupon, a secret
imperial edict was sent to Huá Jiǎo,
ordering him to raise troops in the upper reaches of the river.
The imperial destiny was in peril,
almost falling into the hands of the vile sort.
It even came to enlisting those far and near,
combining forces in Bā and Xiāng,
with factions spreading everywhere,
raiding and disturbing
Yī and Shè.
Another imperial edict commanded Ōuyáng Hè and others to attack and besiege Héngzhōu,
causing turmoil in the Lingnan region,
dragging on for months.
How could his crimes merely exceed those of Chāngyì?
Not only was his reputation more xấu
than during the Tàihé reign.
But though the wicked rascals were all gone
and the demonic followers dispersed,
day by day it was hoped he would repent and reform,
yet he continued to conceal his transgressions,
acting contrary to propriety and forgetting virtue.
His disposition did not change,
delighting in misfortune and thinking
of rebellion,
his depravity endless.
Zhāng Ānguó, a petty, cunning villain,
was reduced to a small-time bandit.
Still, he dispatched an envoy, Jiǎng Yù, to secretly leave the capital,
immediately establishing a provisional government
and selecting
a sinister faction.
The rebel Jiǎo's wife, Lǚ,
who had been made to pound grain as punishment,
was taken from Xīguān
[一二] and hidden in the Yongxiang palace.
She was made to gather her relatives and old acquaintances,
planning to cause harm and disaster.
The local leader Hóu Fǎxǐ and others,
under the Grand Tutor's command,
constantly frequented the imperial court.
They were enticed with great profit,
plotting a rebellion from within.
Just then, the local leader Sūn Tài and others secretly connected
and formed alliances,
with significant communication.
Their military strength was exceptionally strong,
with a set date to stir up trouble.
The imperial house has good fortune,
its mandate long and distant.
Heaven inspired their hearts,
uniformly revealing (the truth).
These
written records
are now shown to you.
If this can be endured,
then who will not tolerate it?
The ancestral foundation and legacy
are feared to be overturned and destroyed.
How can one again solemnly conduct sacrificial rites
and rule the multitude of
people?
Examining past precedents,
he ought to be banished.
Now, he is specifically demoted to Prince of Línhǎi Commandery
and sent back to his princely residence.
The Grand Tutor, Prince Ānchéng, was born with virtue by Heaven,
sagacious, vast, and profound.
Both empresses placed their hearts in him;
the three spirits awaited his favor.
Since the previous emperor fell ill,
he took charge of the nation.
His might and benevolence were widely proclaimed,
punishments and rites were both established.
With his commands and roars,
Xiāng and Yǐng were completely pacified.
Expanding territory and opening frontiers,
Jīng and Yì were swept by his influence.
Like Tàiwù succeeding the Yin dynasty,
or Zhōngdū serving the Han imperial house,
comparing their achievements,
how could they even be similar?
Moreover, the earth revealed an auspicious seal,
and the heavens displayed a long comet.
Renewing the old and removing the corrupt,
all auspicious omens were manifested.
Emperor Wén's discernment in knowing his son
was much like that of Emperor Yáo.
His intention to pass the throne to his younger brother
also matched Tàibó.
Now, his past aspirations can be renewed,
establishing a wise ruler,
thereby solidifying the imperial succession
and aligning with the celestial phenomena.
Officials within and outside the court should follow the old tradition,
respectfully welcome the imperial carriage.
This widow unfortunately faced such deep sorrow.
If there is no rise or fall (of the worthy),
allowing the state to be in peril,
how can I offer obeisance at the lofty shrine
and be interred with Wǔyuán?
Taking up the brush,
I feel both sorrow and joy.
On this day,
(he) moved to another residence.
In the fourth month of the second year of Tàijiàn, (he) died,
at the age of nineteen.
The Emperor was weak and lacked the qualities of a ruler.
Shìzǔ often worried he was unfit to succeed to the throne.
Since he was the legitimate heir,
the matter of deposing or establishing (an emperor) was serious,
hence the long period of indecision.
When his illness became critical,
he summoned Gāozōng and said,
