"I wish to follow the example of Tàibó."
Gāozōng initially did not understand the meaning.
Later, he comprehended,
then prostrated himself, weeping,
firmly declining.
Subsequently, Empress Xuān, following the imperial edict, deposed the Emperor.
The imperial historian says: Although Línhǎi bore the heavy responsibility of succession,
he was kind and gentle,
[一三] mixing right and wrong,
unperturbed by gains or losses.
He was of the same ilk as Emperor Zhì and Emperor Huì of Han.
Shìzǔ knew the gravity of the imperial mandate
and that he would surely find it difficult to bear,
deeply discerning Emperor Yáo's intention,
and thus did not pass on the imperial throne.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals, Part Five, Emperor Xuān
Gāozōng Xiàoxuān Huángdì, personal name Xù,
courtesy name Shàoshì,
childhood name Shīlì,
was the second son of Shǐxīng Zhāoliè Wáng.
He was born on the Xīnyǒu day of the seventh month of the second year of Dàtōng in Liáng [Dynasty],
when a red light filled the entire hall.
As a youth, he was generous and broad-minded,
and possessed great wisdom and strategy.
As he grew older,
he had a beautiful appearance and bearing,
was eight feet three inches tall,
and his hands hung below his knees.
He possessed courage and strength,
and was skilled in horsemanship and archery.
When Gāozǔ pacified Hóu Jǐng
and garrisoned Jīngkǒu,
Liáng Yuándì summoned Gāozǔ's sons and nephews to attend him.
Gāozǔ sent Gāozōng to Jiānglíng,
where he successively held the offices of Zhíhé Jiāngjūn and Zhōngshū Shìláng.
At that time, a cavalry commander, Lǐ Zǒng, who had an old acquaintance with Gāozōng,
often accompanied him.
One night, Gāozōng was drunk,
and fell asleep with a lamp lit.
Zǒng happened to be out,
but soon returned,
and saw Gāozōng's body transform into a great dragon.
Zǒng was immediately startled and terrified,
and fled to another room.
When Jiānglíng fell,
Gāozōng was relocated to Guānyòu.
In the first year of Yǒngdìng,
he was remotely granted the title of Shǐxīng Jùnwáng,
with an income of two thousand households.
In the third year,
Shìzǔ succeeded to the throne,
and he was re-enfeoffed as Ānchéng Wáng.
In the third year of Tiānjīa,
he returned from Zhōu,
and was appointed Shìzhōng, Zhōngshū Jiān, and Zhōngwèi Jiāngjūn,
and given aides.
Soon after, he was appointed Shǐchíjié, Dūdū Yáng Nánxú Dōngyáng Nányù Běijiāng Wǔzhōu Zhūjūnsì, Yángzhōu Cìshǐ,
promoted to Piàojì Jiāngjūn,
with other duties remaining unchanged.
In the fourth year,
he was granted the additional title of Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
In the sixth year,
he was promoted to Sīkōng.
In the first year of Tiānkāng,
he was appointed Shàngshū Lìng,
with all other duties remaining unchanged.
When Fèidì ascended the throne,
he was appointed Sītú,
promoted to Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn,
made Lù Shàngshū,
Dūdū Zhōngwài Zhūjūnsì,
and granted thirty guards with swords.
In the first month of the second year of Guāngdà,
he was promoted to Tàifù,
also holding the position of Sītú,
granted special courtesies,
allowed to wear swords and shoes into the palace,
and his income was increased to three thousand households, including previous ones,
with all other duties remaining unchanged.
On the Jiǎyín day of the eleventh month,
Cíxùn Tàihòu ordered Fèidì to be made Línhǎi Wáng,
and Gāozōng to ascend the throne.
On the Jiǎwǔ day of the first month of spring in the first year of Tàijiàn,
he ascended the imperial throne at the front hall of Tàijí.
An imperial edict stated:
"Indeed, when sages receive the Mandate,
and kings lead a restoration,
it is always due to their excellent virtue
that they become the supreme ruler.
Gāozǔ Wǔhuángdì bowed to the charts of Yáo
and managed the tracks of Yǔ,
his achievement of matching Heaven
illuminated the celestial bodies and brought prosperity and peace;
his merit in establishing the land
was as vast and enduring as rivers and mountains.
Shìzǔ Wénhuángdì possessed the demeanor of a supreme sage,
and met the fortune of pacifying the realm.
He built palaces with frugality,
and his sole pursuit was virtue.
When establishing the initial foundation of the dynasty,
his strategy was always there.
I, being of shallow virtue,
and lacking the talent of sages,
have long carried the burden of former regulations,
and am now to inherit the auspicious legacy.
Although I personally received instruction and teaching,
and wished to uphold the defenses of the realm,
reciting the lofty conduct of Jìzǐ,
and contemplating the distant entrustment of Chéngyáng,
since the crown prince succeeded to the nation
and rightfully assumed the position of ruler,
there has been no wrongdoing in the realm,
and we awaited the cessation of punishments.
How could I have anticipated that the royal house would not prosper,
and that conspiracies of rebellion would repeatedly arise,
the steps of Heaven proving difficult,
threatening to overturn the precious reign?
Reflecting on the auspicious Mandate from above,
it has now fallen upon my person.
My heart is firm and true,
([vacant])[firmly] swearing to the azure heavens.
Yet, all the ministers have earnestly pleaded,
clamoring at Wèiqiáo.
Wénmǔ, with her revered dignity,
has her heart set on Chánglè.
My acceptance of the imperial seal and sash
is not merely the three refusals of Yīn Tāng;
my endurance through spring and winter
is more than the five abdications of Dàiwáng.
Now, I respectfully uphold the celestial decree
and reverently accept the auspicious scepter.
If I base myself on the vast ocean,
my diligence and awe will only increase.
I shall strive to let clouds move and rain fall,
so that all things may prosper,
and share this joy
with the common people.
Therefore, the third year of Guāngdà is to be changed to the first year of Tàijiàn.
A general amnesty is proclaimed throughout the empire.
All civil and military officials in office are promoted one rank.
Those who practice filial piety, brotherly respect, and diligence in farming, as well as those who are successors to their fathers, are granted one noble title.
Those of exceptional talent and unique abilities
are all to be commended.
The widowed, lonely, orphaned, and solitary who cannot support themselves
are each granted five *hú* of grain."
The revered title of Tàihuáng Tàihòu was restored to Huáng Tàihòu.
His consort, Lady Liǔ, was established as empress.
His eldest son, Shúbǎo, was established as crown prince.
His imperial son, Nánzhōngláng Jiāng and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ, Kānglè Hóu Shúlíng, was enfeoffed as Shǐxīng Wáng,

On the Yǐwèi day,

envoys were dispatched to tour the four directions,

Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and newly appointed Zhōngfǔ Dàjiāngjūn Zhāng Zhāodá was promoted to Chējì Dàjiāngjūn.
Newly appointed Zhōngjūn Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ Chúnyú Liáng was made Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn.
Zhènběi Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ, and newly appointed Zhènxī Jiāngjūn and Yǐngzhōu Cìshǐ Huáng Fǎkuàng was promoted to Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn.

"Winning over distant people through virtue

whether they are in the capital cities or various prefectures and garrisons,
regardless of distance,
are all exempt from corvée labor and taxes.
If the old territories are pacified
and our invaded lands returned,
they shall all be permitted to return to their hometowns,
without any restrictions.
The prefects of zhōus, jùns, and xiàns should clearly distinguish them,
and suitable arrangements should be made for them in fertile fields and abandoned villages.
If there are any arbitrary levies or impositions,
it shall be considered disturbing the people. "
Another edict stated:
"The people are the foundation of the state,
as recorded in the canons and plans.
Governing the nation and loving the people
is also a universal teaching.
I attend court early and retire late,
toiling from dawn to dusk,
so that benevolent favor may flow
and spread to the myriad populace.
In the late period of Liáng,
governance and punishment were neglected,
and the regulations and order were chaotic.
Usurpers and bandits rose repeatedly,
and corvée, taxes, and levies
were particularly burdensome and harsh.
The great Chén Dynasty rose
to remedy these lingering evils,
to suppress rebels and quell disturbances.
Without time to innovate and reform,
years passed,
and it became custom.
If not relaxed and eased,
the people will have nowhere to settle.
I am anxious day and night,
feeling as if I have a severe headache.
I wish to live simply
and be frugal to benefit the people.
Although the imperial treasury is not yet full,
what can the ruler do to fully satisfy?
Therefore, these measures should be promptly revised
and their excesses removed,
hoping to establish a lasting standard
that is simple and easy to follow.
From now on, concerning cultivation,
if there is a failed harvest due to floods or droughts,
it should be reported to the local authorities
and submitted for tax reduction.
Soldiers who reach sixty years of age
are all permitted to be discharged and return home.
Skilled artisans who die in service or are old and infirm
do not need to be replaced.
Those who have concealed their skills in the registers,
and all princes, dukes, and officials who have arbitrarily accepted commoners as their retainers
shall return them to their original households,
and an amnesty will be granted for those who surrender themselves.
Those in office handling affairs
must mutually inspect and demonstrate
that there are no omissions or failures to report;
if there are, the officials in charge will be held responsible.
When county magistrates are replaced,
they must provide a detailed list of households that have been discharged
to their successors.
If there is an increase in households,
rewards will be given;
if there is a decrease or dispersion,
penalties will be applied according to the circumstances.
Those who are able to reclaim wasteland,
regardless of the amount,
shall be exempt from taxes as before. "
On the day Wùzǐ,
Táibái (Venus) was seen in daylight.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Sànqí Chángshì, Zhèndōng Jiāngjūn, Wúxìng Tàishǒu Dù Léng was appointed Tèjìn, Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.

In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the kingdom of Gāolì sent an envoy to present local products.
In the twelfth month, on the night of Guǐsì,
there was thunder in the northwest.

Shàngshū Yòupúyè, Lǐng Dàzhùzuò Xú Líng was appointed Shàngshū Púyè.
On the day Xīnyǒu,

On the day Xīnwèi,

From Tiānkāng first year to Tàijiàn first year,

were remitted.
It was also decreed that the sons, younger brothers, and collateral relatives of rebels who had fled to other regions

their residences

In the ninth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Táibái (Venus) was seen in daylight.

Shàngshū Púyè, Lǐng Dàzhùzuò Xú Líng was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒpúyè;

On the day Gēngshēn,

On the day Gēngwǔ,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
In the second month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Imperial Prince Shūqīng was enfeoffed as Jiàn'ān Wáng,
and appointed Dōng Zhōnglángjiāng, Dōngyángzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the third month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Sànqí Chángshì Sūn Yáng was appointed Ānxī Jiāngjūn, Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Yǐchǒu,

In summer, the fourth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Zhōngquán Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī Huáng Fǎqū was appointed Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn, Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Shàngshū Yòupúyè Wáng Mài passed away.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Shìzhōng, Zhèn Yòu Jiāngjūn, Yòu Guānglù Dàfū Dù Léng passed away.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day *Xīnwèi*,
Zhōu sent envoys to seek amity.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
auspicious clouds were seen.
On the day *Wùyín*,
an edict said:
“The great affairs of the state,
involve receiving the sacrificial meat and raising armies.
Troops are dispatched according to regulations,
and strategies are deliberated in the ancestral temple,
thus securing peace throughout the land,
and achieving the seven virtues.
Since recently sweeping away all defilements,
and clearing all of Zhūxià,
it was due to the united efforts of brave warriors,
and also the strategic planning from within the camp.
Although the 'left-lapel' barbarians have been subdued,
and weapons are now sheathed,
Hūhán has come to pay respects,
and there are no alerts at the border outposts;
yet, 'not instructing the people in battle is called abandoning them,'
benevolence must be accompanied by courage,
and military preparedness must not be forgotten.
Jiāng Tài Gōng transmitted his military secrets at Pánxī,
and Huángshí Gōng bestowed the divine talisman at Gǔchéng.
Guāng Wǔ Dì formulated military regulations from afar,
and Cáo Cāo frequently spoke of military strategies.
I, though ashamed of my own lack of insight,
have genuinely perused all of these.
Furthermore, having personally overseen military campaigns in the past,
I have thoroughly experienced the drills and formations.
Organizing them into seven paces,
and disciplining them with three drum rolls,
I gained this from my own understanding,
and can describe it clearly.
Now I have compiled these regulations,
totaling thirteen articles,
which should be immediately promulgated,
to serve as a permanent standard.”
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
an edict ordered the suspension of outstanding rents for Xiāngzhōu and Jiāngzhōu,
and for the displaced people of Wúxī and fifteen other counties,
all their labor and taxes were remitted.
(Autumn)
In the ninth month, on the day *Gēngzǐ* (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *Xīnhài*,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Another edict said:
“Promoting the good and accepting remonstrance
are the clear guidelines for those above;
advancing the virtuous and presenting advice
are the exemplary models for ministers.
I, with my meager virtue,
have succeeded to guard the imperial inheritance.
Though the world has long been peaceful under our dynasty,
my rule has not been entirely stable.
Distinguishing directions and assigning duties,
I have worked from dawn till dusk;
yet, there are no remonstrating ministers at the palace gates,
and no meritorious scholars from below.
How can this be lacking,
with few able to speak out directly?
Is it that I act alone,
and do not seek honest advice?
A drum is placed at the Gōngchē,
but seldom are gains and losses discussed;
stones are placed at the Xiàngwèi,
but no one presents what is feasible or not.
I have not encountered anyone like Zhū Yún, who broke the imperial palanquin;
nor is it common to find one like Qín Xī, who struck the pillar.
As for those who appear in coarse clothes,
or wander with their bamboo hats and umbrellas,
some are elders of peerless wisdom,
others are youths of extraordinary talent,
but they are ill-suited to the times,
and are not praised by those around them.
Their black sables become worn,
and their gold is depleted,
ultimately they remain obscure,
which is truly lamentable.
Furthermore, there are hundreds of high-ranking officials,
and ten grades of lower officials.
The skilled and the unskilled are equally promoted,
and encouragement and discouragement are indistinguishable.
Street rumors merely accumulate,
and court discussions are deficient.
This is truly due to my lack of clarity,
and the absence of those who offer improvements or criticisms.
Reflecting on perfect governance,
how can it be so amiss?
This can be communicated to both civil and military officials:
all those in their positions,
if moral transformation deviates,
or court administration becomes corrupted,
should speak with integrity and directness,
offending without concealment.
Moreover, each should recommend those they know,
and their talents should be clearly tested.
Their integrity or corruption in governance,
and their competence or incompetence in office,
should be separately reported with truth,
awaiting their demotion or promotion.”
On the day *Jǐngyín* (Gēngyín),
the late Grand Commandant Xú Dù, Minister-Supervisor Dù Léng, and Minister-Supervisor Chéng Língxǐ were accorded joint sacrifice in the ancestral temple of Gāozǔ;
the late General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhāng Zhāodá was accorded joint sacrifice in the ancestral temple of Shìzǔ.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *Yǐyǒu*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
On the day *Wùxū*,
Shěn Kè, General Who Guards the South and Governor of Guǎngzhōū, was appointed General of the Imperial Guard.
In the eleventh month, on the night of *Jǐhài*, there was an earthquake.
In the intercalary month, on the day *Xīnwèi*,
an edict said:
“Gūshú is vast and open,
comparable to Jīnghé.
Bówàng and its environs,
are naturally formidable.
Lóngshān points south,
Niúzhǔ overlooks the north,
facing the remains of Xióng Yì's city,
and near Quán Cóng's old fortress.
With fertile fields and beautiful mulberries,
the ridges and furrows stretch as far as the eye can see,
contiguous houses with high roofs,
and roads like embroidery.
Since the military disasters at the end of Liáng dynasty,
it has been almost completely devastated.
Although efforts have been made to provide generous relief,
it has not yet been fully restored.
As it is close to the capital region,
it should be prosperous and abundant.
Furthermore, many subordinates of the various generals
have settled in the upper and lower regions,
with a mixture of military and civilian populations,
which has caused great harm and depletion.
From now on, those who are dismissed from their posts
are permitted to have their subordinates remain;
those already outside of Jiāngnán
should also be welcomed back,
and all settled in the southern districts of the province.
Whether exchanging goods or not,
they will not be charged market value;
for reclaiming and cultivating barren land,
rent and taxes will also be suspended.
The Court will dispatch one鎮監 (zhènjiān)
to clearly inspect and manage together with the Governor and the 津主 (jīnzhǔ),
distributing land and assigning fields,
and each establishing their residences.”
In the twelfth month, on the day *Rényín*,
sweet dew descended upon the Lèyóu Gardens.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
the imperial carriage visited the Lèyóu Gardens,
collected the sweet dew,
and held a banquet for the officials.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
an edict said:
“At the end of the Liáng dynasty,
wars and fires repeatedly occurred,
the Chénghuá Palace was burned and destroyed,
leaving no trace.
Since the renewal of the imperial mandate,
nearly two decades have passed,
with frequent military campaigns,
leaving no time for repairs.
Now that military work is relatively light,
and timbers are prepared,
construction will begin next year,
to establish the Eastern Palace.
A Provisional Minister of Works and Grand Architect should be appointed,
to oversee the construction.”
In the fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Chúnyú Liáng, General Who Conquers the North, *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, and Governor of Nánsúzhōu, was appointed General of the Central Command;
Shěn Shūyīng, General Who Spreads Benevolence and Prince of Yùzhāng, was appointed Governor of Nánsúzhōu,
and promoted to the title General Who Pacifies the North;
Shěn Jūnlǐ, Minister of Personnel and Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, was appointed Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs,
and concurrently in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
On the day *Xīnsì*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburbs.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
In the second month, on the day *Xīnchǒu*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Bright Hall.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,

pierced the Zǐgōng of the Northern Dipper from the north.
In the third month, on the day *Rénwǔ*,
orders were issued to the various armies for a northern expedition,
with Wú Míngchè, General Who Guards the Front and *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, appointed Supreme Commander of all punitive expeditionary forces.
On the day *Jǐngxū* (Gēngxū),
Xīhéngzhōu presented a horse born with horns.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the imperial grandson Yìn was born.
Civil and military officials, both inside and outside the court, were granted silk with varying amounts,
and those who succeeded their fathers were promoted one rank.
Wú Míngchè, the Grand Commander of the Northern Expedition, led an army of 100,000,
departing from Báixià.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the former Bāzhōu Cìshǐ, Lǔ Guǎngdá, captured Qídàxiànchéng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Wú Míngchè captured Qínzhōu Shuǐzhà.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Qí sent ten thousand soldiers to reinforce Lìyáng,

On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Qí army rescued Qínzhōu,

On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict ordered that all Qí soldiers killed by the northern expeditionary forces
should be buried.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Nánqiáo Tàishǒu Xú Màn captured Shíliángchéng.

On the day Guǐyǒu,

On the day Jiǎxū,

On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Huáng Fǎlú captured Lìyángchéng.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Běigāotáng Jùnchéng surrendered.
On the day Xīnsì,
an imperial edict ordered Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ Huáng Fǎlú to move his garrison to Lìyáng,

On the day Yǐyǒu,
Nánqíchāng Tàishǒu Huáng Yǒng captured Qíchāng Wàichéng.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Lúlíng Nèishǐ Rèn Zhōng's army reached Dōngguān,

On the day Wùzǐ,
he also captured Qiáojùnchéng,
and Qínzhōuchéng surrendered.
On the day Guǐsì,
Guābù and Húshù, two cities, surrendered.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Yǐngzhōu Cìshǐ Lǐ Zōng captured Shèkǒuchéng.
On the day Yǐsì,
Rèn Zhōng captured Hézhōu Wàichéng.
On the day Gēngxū,
Huáiyáng and Shùyáng Commandery both abandoned their cities and fled.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Auspicious Clouds appeared.
Yùzhāng Nèishǐ Chéng Wénjì captured Jīngzhōuchéng.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Xuānyì Sīmǎ Zhàn captured Xīncàichéng.
On the day Guǐhài,
Zhōu sent envoys to pay tribute.
〔一二〕Huáng Fǎlú captured Hézhōuchéng.
Wú Míngchè's army arrived at Rénzhōu,

This month,
the Míngtáng was constructed.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Zhènqián Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī Wú Míngchè was promoted to Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn.
On the day Wùchén,

Wú Míngchè's army arrived at Xiákǒu,

The gentry and commoners of Huáiběi Jiàngchéng and Gǔyáng
executed their leaders

On the day Bǐngxū,
Wú Míngchè captured Shòuyáng Wàichéng.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Shānyángchéng surrendered.

Xūyíchéng surrendered.

Pínggù Hóu Chén Jìngtài and others captured Jìnzhōuchéng.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Yángpíngchéng surrendered.
〔一三〕On the day Rénshēn,
Gāotáng Tàishǒu Shěn Shàndù captured Mǎtóuchéng.
〔一四〕On the day Jiǎxū,
Qí'ānchéng surrendered.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn Fán Yì captured Guǎnglíng Chǔzǐchéng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Shàngshū Yòupúshè, Lǐng Lìbù, Fùmǎ Dūwèi Shěn Jūnlǐ passed away.
On the day Dīnghài,
the former Póyáng Nèishǐ Lǔ Tiānnìan captured Huángchéng Xiǎochéng,
and the Qí army retreated to defend Dàchéng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Xūyí Jùn of Nánpìzhōu was detached and assigned to Qiáozhōu.
On the last day of the month, Rénchén,
there was a night illumination.
Huángchéng Dàchéng surrendered.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Guōmòchéng surrendered.
On the day Wùxū,
Zhōngshū Lìng Wáng Yáng was appointed Lìbù Shàngshū.
On the day Jǐhài,
Tèjìn, Lǐng Guózǐ Jìjiǔ Zhōu Hóngzhèng was appointed Shàngshū Yòupúshè.
On the day Yǐsì,
Wú Míngchè captured Shòuyángchéng,
beheaded Wáng Lín,
sent his head to the capital,
and displayed it on Zhùquè Háng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
ten thousand Qí soldiers reached Yǐngkǒu,
but Fán Yì attacked and repelled them.
On the day Xīnhài,
Qí sent troops to reinforce Cānglíng,
but they were again defeated.
On the day Bǐngchén,
an imperial edict stated:
“At the end of Liáng, Xuánhù was obtained,
and Shòuyáng was made Nányùzhōu;
now that it has been recovered,
it can be restored to Yùzhōu.
Huángchéng shall be Sīzhōu,
its governing seat will be Ānchāng Jùn,
Chǎntuān will be Hànyáng Jùn,
and the three cities according to Liáng will be Yìyáng Jùn,
all belonging to Sīzhōu.”
Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī Wú Míngchè was appointed Yùzhōu Cìshǐ,
and promoted to Chējì Dàjiāngjūn;
Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ Huáng Fǎlú was appointed Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn, Hézhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Zhàn captured Qíchāngchéng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Huáiyīnchéng surrendered.
On the day Gēngchén,
Wēilǔ Jiāngjūn Liú Táogēn captured Qúshānchéng.
〔一五〕On the day Xīnsì,
Fán Yì captured Jìyīnchéng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Lǔ Guǎngdá and others captured Běixúzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the first day, Rénchén,
an imperial edict stated:
“In ancient times, those who rebelled and betrayed
were completely exterminated,
their heads were hidden to
warn future generations.
Recently, only the individual himself has been executed,
and his descendants may survive;
displaying the heads is sufficient,
they should not remain long in the armory,
or forever compared to the Yuèzhī.
I have a feeling of compassion,
and a benevolent heart cannot bear it.
Therefore, the heads of Xióng Tánlǎng, Liú Yì, Chén Bǎo'yìng, Zhōu Dí, Dèng Xù, etc., and now Wáng Lín's head,
shall all be returned to their relatives,
to demonstrate broad clemency.”
On the day Yǐwèi,
Qiáochéng surrendered.
On the day Yǐsì,
Imperial Prince Shūmíng was enfeoffed as Yídū Wáng,
and Shūxiàn as Hédōng Wáng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Rèn Zhōng captured Huòzhōuchéng.
In the spring, the first month, on the *gēng-chén* day of the eighth year [of the Tài-Jiàn reign],
a purple cloud was seen in the southwest.
In the second month, on the *rén-shēn* day,
Chē-Qí Dà-Jiàng-Jūn (Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry) and Kāi-Fǔ Yí-Tóng Sān-Sī (Minister of the Bureau of Administration) Wú Míng-Chè (吳明徹) was promoted to Sī-Kōng (Minister of Works).
On the *dīng-chǒu* day,
an imperial edict pardoned all outstanding summer taxes and tributes from before the fifth year of Tài-Jiàn in the Jiāng-Dōng region
that were still owed by the common people.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎ-yín* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The grand marshal has returned victorious,
and the armies have triumphantly concluded their campaign.
To celebrate their achievements and reward their merits,
a banquet is fitting.
On the seventeenth day of this month,
We shall proceed to Lè-Yóu Yuàn (樂遊苑),
where music will be played
and a grand gathering of civil and military officials will be held.”
On the *jǐ-wèi* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Tài-Miào (太廟) (Grand Ancestral Temple).
【Fifth Month】On the *gēng-yín* day,
Shàng-Shū Zuǒ-Pú-Shè (Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs) Wáng Yáng (王瑒) died.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐ-chǒu* day,
Yún-Huī Jiàng-Jūn (General of Cloud-like Brilliance) and Guǎng-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ (刺史) (Governor of Guǎng-Zhōu) Cháng-Shā Wáng Shū-Jiān (長沙王叔堅) was appointed Hé-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ (Governor of Hé-Zhōu)
and promoted to Píng-Běi Jiàng-Jūn (General Who Pacifies the North).
On the *jiǎ-yín* day,
Shàng-Shū Yòu-Pú-Shè (Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs) Lù Sàn (陸繕) was appointed Shàng-Shū Zuǒ-Pú-Shè,
and the newly appointed Jìn-Líng Tài-Shǒu (太守) (Administrator of Jìn-Líng) Wáng Kè (王克) was appointed Shàng-Shū Yòu-Pú-Shè.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the *dīng-mǎo* day,
Chē-Qí Dà-Jiàng-Jūn and Sī-Kōng Wú Míng-Chè was appointed Nán-Yùn-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ (Governor of Nán-Yùn-Zhōu).
In the ninth month, on the *wù-xū* day,
Imperial Prince Shū-Biāo (叔彪) was enfeoffed as Huái-Nán Wáng (淮南王) (King of Huái-Nán).
In the winter, the eleventh month, on the *yǐ-yǒu* day,

Píng-Nán Jiàng-Jūn (General Who Pacifies the South) and Xiāng-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ Cháng-Shā Wáng Shū-Jiān was appointed Píng-Xī Jiàng-Jūn (General Who Pacifies the West) and Yǐng-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ (Governor of Yǐng-Zhōu).
On the *dīng-yǒu* day,
the three commanderies of Jìn-Xī (晉熙), Gāo-Táng (高唐), and Xīn-Cài (新蔡) in Jiāng-Zhōu (江州) were separated to form Jìn-Zhōu (晉州).
On the *xīn-chǒu* day,
Guān-Jūn Jiàng-Jūn (General of the Champion Army) Lú-Líng Wáng Bó-Rén (廬陵王伯仁) was appointed Zhōng-Lǐng-Jūn (Commander of the Central Army).
In the twelfth month, on the *dīng-mǎo* day,
the newly appointed Tài-Zǐ Zhān-Shì (太子詹事) (Chief Minister of the Crown Prince's Household) Xú Líng (徐陵) was appointed Yòu-Guāng-Lù Dà-Fū (右光祿大夫) (Grand Master of Remonstrance of the Right).
In the spring, the first month, on the *xīn-mǎo* day of the ninth year,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the northern suburban altar.
On the *rén-yín* day,
Xiāng-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ and the newly appointed Zhōng-Wèi Jiàng-Jūn (General of the Central Guard) Shǐ-Xīng Wáng Shū-Líng (始興王叔陵) was appointed Yáng-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ (Governor of Yáng-Zhōu);
Yún-Huī Jiàng-Jūn Jiàn-Ān Wáng Shū-Qīng (建安王叔卿) was appointed Xiāng-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ,
and promoted to Píng-Nán Jiàng-Jūn.
In the second month, on the *rén-zǐ* day,
the imperial carriage personally plowed the ceremonial field.
In the summer, the fifth month, on the *gěng-zǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“We rise at dawn to don Our robes,
and only eat late in the day,
pondering how to broaden the welfare of the myriad people
and bring about order.
However, the regional governors and administrators overseeing the people
have not fully ensured integrity and fairness.
The annual rents and tributes
often result in arrears.
Therefore, in this matter of farming,
leniency and remission should be broadly applied.
All outstanding rents and tributes owed by migrants and rebellious households from the beginning of Tài-Jiàn to the eighth year,

the rebellious soldiers (義丁) of the seventh and eighth years, the rebellious military laborers (軍丁) from the fifth to the eighth year, and the outstanding land-rice, millet, summer tribute (綿絹絲布麥) of silk floss, silk fabric, raw silk, cloth, and wheat for the sixth and seventh years,
as well as
the outstanding silk tribute (貲絹) from the fifth to the seventh year,
are all hereby pardoned.”
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *yǐ-hài* day,
Qīng-Chē Jiàng-Jūn (General of Light Chariots) and Dān-Yáng Yǐn (丹陽尹) (Administrator of Dān-Yáng) Jiāng-Xià Wáng Bó-Yì (江夏王伯義) was appointed Hé-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ.
On the *jǐ-mǎo* day,
the kingdom of Bǎi-Jì (百濟) sent envoys to offer local products.
On the *gēng-chén* day,
there was heavy rain and lightning struck the ornamental pillar of Wàn-Ān Líng (萬安陵).
On the *jǐ-chǒu* day,

lightning struck the pagoda finial of Huì-Rì Sì (慧日寺) and the dew-plate of Zhuāng-Yán Sì (莊嚴寺), the east tower of Chóng-Yáng Gé (重陽閣), a pagoda tree inside Qiān-Qiū Mén (千秋門), and the gate of Hóng-Lú Fǔ (鴻臚府);
a woman standing under the gate was struck dead.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *wù-wǔ* day,
Sī-Kōng Wú Míng-Chè defeated Zhōu (周) general Liáng Shì-Yàn’s (梁士彥) army of tens of thousands at Lǚ-Liáng (呂梁).
In the twelfth month, on the *wù-shēn* day,
the Eastern Palace was completed,
and the Crown Prince moved into the new palace.
In the spring, the first month, on the *jǐ-sì* day, the first day of the tenth year,
Zhōng-Lǐng-Jūn Lú-Líng Wáng Bó-Rén was appointed Píng-Běi Jiàng-Jūn and Nán-Xú-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ (Governor of Nán-Xú-Zhōu);

Yì-Zuǒ Jiàng-Jūn (General of the Left Flank), Yòu-Guāng-Lù Dà-Fū, and Lǐng Tài-Zǐ Zhān-Shì (Chief Minister of the Crown Prince's Household) Xú Líng was appointed Lǐng-Jūn Jiàng-Jūn (Commander of the Army).
In the second month, on the *jiǎ-zǐ* day,
the northern expeditionary armies suffered a defeat at Lǚ-Liáng,
and Sī-Kōng Wú Míng-Chè, along with his generals and soldiers,
were all captured by the Zhōu army.
In the third month, on the *xīn-wèi* day,
lightning struck the Military Arsenal (Wǔ-Kù).
On the *gěng-zǐ* day,

various armies were dispatched to prepare for Zhōu: Zhōng-Jūn Dà-Jiàng-Jūn (Grand General of the Central Army), Kāi-Fǔ Yí-Tóng Sān-Sī Chún-Yú Liàng (淳于量) was appointed Dà Dū-Dū (大都督) (Grand Commander),
in charge of all land and naval forces;
Míng-Wēi Jiàng-Jūn (General of Illustrious Might) Sūn Yáng (孫瑒) was appointed Dū-Dū Jīng-Yǐng Shuǐ-Lù Zhū-Jūn Shì (都督荊、郢水陸諸軍事) (Supervisor of All Land and Naval Forces of Jīng and Yǐng),
and promoted to Zhèn-Xī Jiàng-Jūn (General Who Guards the West);
Zuǒ-Wèi Jiàng-Jūn (General of the Left Guard) Fán Yì (樊毅) was appointed Dà Dū-Dū,
supervising the various armies along the Huái River from Zhū-Pèi (朱沛) and Qīng-Kǒu (清口) up to Jīng-Shān (荊山),
and promoted to Píng-Běi Jiàng-Jūn;

Wǔ-Yì Jiàng-Jūn (General of Martial Might) Rèn Zhōng (任忠) was appointed Dū-Dū Shòu-Yáng Xīn-Cài Huò-Zhōu Děng Zhòng-Jūn (都督壽陽、新蔡、霍州等衆軍) (Supervisor of the Armies of Shòu-Yáng, Xīn-Cài, Huò-Zhōu, etc.),
and promoted to Níng-Yuǎn Jiàng-Jūn (General Who Pacifies Distant Lands).
On the *yǐ-yǒu* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the *dīng-yǒu* day,
Zhōng-Jūn Dà-Jiàng-Jūn, Kāi-Fǔ Yí-Tóng Sān-Sī, and Hù-Jūn Jiàng-Jūn (Protector General) Chún-Yú Liàng was appointed Nán-Yùn-Zhōu Cì-Shǐ,
and promoted to Chē-Qí Jiàng-Jūn (General of Chariots and Cavalry).
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *gēng-xū* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Words of generous rewards
are clear in edicts and proclamations,
and the virtue of compassion
is demonstrated through care and inspection.
In recent years, light campaigns
have cleared the Huái and Sī Rivers.
With sharp thrusts, achievements were made,
and both civil and military officials exerted their utmost strength.
Braving wind and rain,
and enduring frequent changes of cold and heat,
Our thoughts are on their merits,
never forgetting them even when eating.
It is fitting to bestow honors and rewards
to compensate for their toil.
Those serving in the army shall all be granted two ranks of nobility,
and additionally given gratuities and relief.
The selection process shall immediately determine their placements.”
Another imperial edict stated:
“Yáo (堯) wore simple hemp and deerskin clothes,
and was considered great by Heaven.
Bó-Yǔ (伯禹) wore worn clothes and ate simple food,
and the Master said, ‘There is nothing to criticize.’
Thus, respectful moderation
rarely leads to error.
We have ruled the universe for ten years,
working from late morning without rest,
and forgetting sleep in the late hours of the night,
stretching Our neck in anticipation of good governance,
as if crossing a great river.
Our thoughts are ever on this,
trembling as if driving rotten reins.
It is not for the wealth of the four seas
nor for the veneration of the imperial throne
that We guide benevolence and longevity to the populace,
nor to accumulate labor and toil for Our own benefit.
However, since the end of the Liáng (梁) dynasty,
the suffering from chaos and displacement
has left palaces and fields of grain
named but vanished.
Although splendid buildings are yet unseen,
some construction has been undertaken.
Even after removing excess and extravagance,
it remains a labor and expense.
Furthermore, military expeditions have been frequent,
losing a thousand *jīn* daily,
the treasury is not yet full,
and the people are exhausted by taxes and levies.
If the common people are not sufficient,
how can the ruler be sufficient?
Reflecting on this in quiet thought,
We are anxious night and day,
and feel deeply ashamed
of the instructions We have given and the laws We have enacted.
To hew carving into plainness
is perhaps an admirable goal.
Since the feathered caps have been burned,
hempen clothes shall now be worn.
The regulations for reduction and removal
shall begin with Our own person,
hoping that like grass bending to the wind,
customs will change.
Beyond the ritual music, ceremonial attire, and military equipment
to be constructed by the imperial workshops and offices,
all other projects shall be suspended.
The regular provisions for the imperial concubines and the stipends and allowances for princes, marquises, consorts, and princesses
shall all be proportionately reduced.”
On the *dīng-sì* day,
the newly appointed Zhèn-Yòu Jiàng-Jūn (General Who Guards the Right) Xīn-Ān Wáng Bó-Gù (新安王伯固) was appointed Hù-Jūn Jiàng-Jūn.
On the *wù-wǔ* day,
Fán Yì dispatched troops to cross north of the Huái River and build a city opposite Qīng-Kǒu.
On the *gēng-shēn* day,
there was heavy rain and hail.
On the *rén-xū* day,
the city at Qīng-Kǒu could not be held.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎ-shēn* day,
Tài-Bái (Venus) was seen during the daytime.
In the sixth month, on the *dīng-mǎo* day,

there was heavy rain and lightning struck the pagoda finial of Dà-Huáng Sì (大皇寺), the dew-plate of Zhuāng-Yán Sì, the east tower of Chóng-Yáng Gé, the pagoda tree inside Qiān-Qiū Mén, and the gate of Hóng-Lú Fǔ.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *wù-xū* day,
the kingdom of Xīn-Luó (新羅) sent envoys to offer local products.
On the *yǐ-sì* day,
Sàn-Qí Cháng-Shì (侍) (Counsellor Gentleman-in-Waiting) and concurrent Lì-Bù Shàng-Shū (吏部尚書) (Minister of Personnel) Yuán Xiàn (袁憲) was appointed Lì-Bù Shàng-Shū.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐ-chǒu* day, the first day of the month,
Qín-Jùn (秦郡) was renamed Yì-Zhōu (義州).
On the *wù-yín* day,
frost fell,
killing the rice and beans.
In the ninth month, on the day Rén-yín,
Fán Yì (樊毅), General of Pacifying the North, was appointed Central Leader of the Army.
On the day Yǐ-sì,
a Fāngmíng Altar (方明壇) was established at Lóuhú (婁湖).
On the day Wù-shēn,
Shǐxīng Wáng Shūlíng (始興王叔陵), General of the Central Guard and Governor of Yángzhōu, was concurrently appointed Bó (伯) of Wángguān (王官) to oversee the oath.
On the day Jiǎ-yín,
the imperial carriage proceeded to Lóuhú to supervise the oath.
On the day Yǐ-mǎo,
envoys were dispatched to broadcast the oath throughout the four directions,
so that all, high and low, would be mutually vigilant.
On the day Rén-xū,
Jiāngxià Wáng Bóyì (江夏王伯義), General of Spreading Benevolence, was appointed Governor of Dōngyángzhōu.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wù-yín,
Yìzhōu (義州) and the two commanderies of Lángyá (琅邪) and Péngchéng (彭城) were abolished.
Jiànxīng (建興) was established,
administering the six counties of Jiàn'ān (建安), Tóngxià (同夏), Wūshān (烏山), Jiāngchéng (江乘), Línyí (臨沂), and Húshú (湖熟),
subordinate to Yángzhōu.
On the day Wù-zǐ,
Lù Sàn (陸繕), Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīn-chǒu,
Sūn Yáng (孫瑒), General of Pacifying the West, was appointed Governor of Yǐngzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐ-hài,
Tián Bóxīng (田伯興), a Man (蠻) from Lújiāng (廬江) in Hézhōu (合州), raided Cóngyáng (樅陽).
The governor, Lǔ Guǎngdá (魯廣達), suppressed him.
In the eleventh year, spring, the first month, on the day Dīng-yóu,
a dragon was seen in a pond beside the Yǒngníng (永寧) Tower in Nányǔnzhōu (南兗州).
In the second month, on the day Guǐ-hài,
the imperial carriage personally ploughed the sacrificial field.
In the third month, on the day Dīng-wèi,
an imperial edict was issued for the righteous people north of the Huái River who returned to the state with their households,
to establish their original old names,
set up prefectures and counties,
and immediately attach them to nearby prefectures,
grant them fields and residences,
and ensure that no summons or agreements would involve them.
【Summer】In the fifth month, on the day Yǐ-sì,
〔二五〕an imperial edict stated:
“In the past, Xuānyuán (軒轅) commanded Fēnghòu (風后) and Lìmù (力牧);
Fàngxūn (放勛) consulted Yī Jì (稷), Xiè (契), and Zhū Wǔ (朱武);
〔二六〕wearing the ceremonial crown and folding their hands,
they brought about great peace.
Coming to the Hàn dynasty, five bureaus were established;
the Zhōu dynasty divided into six offices.
Officials were appointed to manage affairs,
each with their specific responsibilities.
It was hoped that punishments would be abolished,
and generations would endure eternally,
all relying on numerous talents
to achieve prosperous accomplishments.
I toil from dawn to dusk,
desiring to promote important governance,
yet state affairs remain obstructed,
and the path of government is unsettled.
Anxious in my heart every night,
I know not how to achieve success.
I now wish to rely on these boats and oars,
entrusting accomplishment to my trusted officials,
demanding substance corresponding to titles,
to seek peace from many virtuous individuals.
From now on, all documents from the Department of State Affairs, various offices, ministries, and imperial secretariats,
shall be submitted to the bureaus for discussion and deliberation.
Matters concerning military and state construction, levies, appointments, and the three prisons,
must first be thoroughly reviewed and decided,
before being reported to me.
In all judgments and decisions,
it is essential to ensure clarity and order,
adhering to laws and regulations,
as clear and uniform as if drawn with a single stroke.
There must be no discrepancies or contradictions between earlier and later rulings,
which would create internal conflict
and lead to injustice or stagnation.
If anyone bends the law or manipulates documents,
their actions will be investigated and known,
and there will be no pardon.”
On the day Jiǎ-yín,
an imperial edict stated:
“The old law considered the crime of taking bribes by distorting the law to be severe,
but the punishment for accepting bribes while upholding the law was very light.
How could this not encourage greed and cruelty,
and give rise to manipulation?
Matters involving money, how can they not be treated with particular severity?
Now, those who accept bribes without distorting the law
shall have their punishment
made equivalent to that for serious theft.”
In the sixth month, on the day Gēng-chén,
Yùzhāng Wáng Shūyīng (豫章王叔英), General of the Vanguard, was appointed General of the South and Governor of Jiāngzhōu.
On the day Jǐng-xū,
Póyáng Wáng Bóshān (鄱陽王伯山), General of Conquering the South and Governor of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed General of the Central Authority and Protector-General of the Army.
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xīn-mǎo,
the large currency, the six-zhū coin (六銖錢), was first used.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎ-zǐ,
Zhū Xiǎnzōng (朱顯宗) and other righteous leaders from Qīngzhōu (青州) led their seven hundred households to surrender and join.
On the day Dīng-mǎo,
the imperial carriage proceeded to Dàzhuàngguān (大壯觀) to review military exercises.
On the day Wù-yín,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiǎ-xū,
Jìn'ān Wáng Bógōng (晉安王伯恭), General of Pacifying the Front and Minister of the Bureau of Sacrifices, was appointed General of the Army Adviser;
Lù Sàn (陸繕), Minister of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīn-mǎo,
an imperial edict stated:
“To avoid violating the 'painted cap' (law),
change this degenerate custom;
to tread upon 'slavery and execution',
transform this shallow practice.
I respectfully received the precious mandate,
and it has now been one cycle (twelve years).
I have sought to govern the state and manage affairs,
worried for the country and loved the people,
toiling from dawn to dusk,
and sacrificing sleep after midnight.
Yet, to return to purity and simplicity,
the path has no steps;
to achieve flourishing beauty and harmony,
none can claim success.
Consequently, the dossiers of interrogation
fill my sight and hearing,
and the number of those condemned to hard labor
overwhelms the prisons.
The Zhōu (周) King Chéng (成) abolished punishments,
and the Hàn (漢) Emperor Wén (文) resolved legal cases –
these examples of empty toil
are now far distant.
Moreover, petty enemies
have encroached upon our Péng (彭) and Biàn (汴) regions;
the populace of Huái (淮) and Rǔ (汝)
eagerly awaits royal strategies.
Mobilizing troops,
the intention is to rescue them.
Transporting fodder and grain,
levies are quite burdensome.
In hot rains and bitter cold,
how can I forget their grievances?
Furthermore, the celestial conjunctions are askew,
and the stations deviate from their proper positions.
The warnings of 'If I say so'
assign blame to the sovereign.
My heart is filled with shame;
I am not afraid of holding onto something decaying.
Now, as the month Jiànzǐ (建子) begins,
the faint Yang energy stirs.
In response to this auspicious time,
it is fitting to spread broad grace.
Therefore, a great amnesty is proclaimed throughout the empire.”
On the day Jiǎ-wǔ,
Zhōu (周) dispatched Zhùguó (柱國) Liáng Shìyàn (梁士彥) to lead his forces to Féikǒu (肥口).
On the day Wù-xū,
the Zhōu army advanced and besieged Shòuyáng (壽陽).
On the day Xīn-chǒu,
Chúnyú Liáng (淳于量), General of Chariots and Cavalry, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (開府儀同三司), and Governor of Nányǔnzhōu (南兗州), was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Upstream Naval Forces;
Fán Yì (樊毅), Central Leader of the Army, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all forces for the Northern Expedition,
and given the added title of General of Pacifying the North;
Rèn Zhōng (任忠), Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard forces for the Northern Expedition,
and given the added title of General of Pacifying the North;
Gāo Wénzòu (皐文奏), former Governor of Fēngzhōu (豐州), led three thousand infantry and cavalry to Qūyángpíng (趣陽平) Commandery.
On the day Guǐ-mǎo,
Rèn Zhōng (任忠) led seven thousand infantry and cavalry to Qínjùn (秦郡).
On the day Jǐng-wǔ,
Lǔ Guǎngdá (魯廣達), newly appointed General of Awe-inspiring Might and General of the Right Guard, led his forces into the Huái River.
On this day,
Fán Yì (樊毅) led twenty thousand naval forces from Dōngguān (東關) into Jiāohú (焦湖);
Xiāo Móhē (蕭摩訶), General of Martial Might, led infantry and cavalry to Lìyáng (歷陽).
On the day Wù-shēn,
Yùzhōu (豫州) fell.
On the day Xīn-hài,
Huòzhōu (霍州) also fell.
On the day Guǐ-chǒu,
Shǐxīng Wáng Shūlíng (始興王叔陵), newly appointed Grand General of the Central Guard and Governor of Yángzhōu, was appointed Grand Commander-in-Chief,
overall commander of all naval and infantry forces.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
the three prefectures of Nánliùyǔn, and Jìn,
as well as the nine commanderies of Xūyí, Shānyáng, Yángpíng, Mătóu, Qín, Lìyáng, Pèi, Bĕiqiáo, and Nánliáng,
Qiáo and Bĕixú Prefectures were again lost.
From this point, all the lands south of the Huái River were lost to the Zhōu.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“In ancient times, Yáo and Shùn were on the throne,
living in thatched huts with earthen steps.
Tāng and Yǔ were rulers,
using staffs of common weeds and belts of deerskin.
As for brocade tents with pearl nets,
magnificent rafters and jade pendants,
these could not bring peace and prosperity,
only speak of extravagance and desire.
I look up to the ancient sages with admiration,
and wish to achieve justice and fairness.
The righteous path is often violated,
and corrupt customs are not corrected.
To this day, the wealthy and powerful families
have golden door-studs and jade shoes,
while the poor in humble alleys
eat pig's food and wear cattle blankets.
To distribute things fairly according to need
seems so distant.
all withdrew themselves and returned to the capital.
and labor and taxes are burdensome.
Corrupt officials are greedy,
arbitrarily imposing regulations.
Furthermore, the watchtowers and market gates
levy excessive taxes.
This does not expand the capital's wealth,
nor does it cover the expenses of the Waterways Office;
instead, it restricts merchants
and enables private hoarding.
Reflecting on these numerous弊,
it is fitting to make reforms.
If the Kingly Way is not broadened,
how can the people's suffering be relieved?
Therefore, it is hereby proclaimed to the Director of the Wardrobe, the Directorate for Imperial Manufactories, and other offices,
that unless it is for military or state necessities,
no new items shall be manufactured.
If there are any superfluous personnel in the imperial harem's ranks,
upon presentation by the Department of the Palace,
they shall all be appropriately dismissed.
Grand performances and secret plays
do not conform to ritual classics,
and the entertainers of the Music Bureau
do not align with refined propriety;
all these shall be revised.
Market assessments and ferry taxes,
military orders and state statutes,
must be reviewed and re-established,
with the sole aim of fairness.
Remote palaces and detached residences,
located in the countryside,
shall not be repaired
unless for regular banquets.
Furthermore, all civil and military officials, both inside and outside the court,
as well as their carriages, horses, and residences,
shall practice frugality
and not indulge in extravagance.
Those who violate my strict regulations
shall be subject to legal punishment.
The relevant authorities shall formulate specific articles and regulations,
post and proclaim them,
so that my intentions may be understood.”
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Shěn Kè, General Who Pacifies the North, and Péi Zĭliè, General Who Electrifies Might, were dispatched to garrison Nánxú Prefecture.
Xú Dàonú, General Who Extends Afar, was dispatched to garrison Shàkŏu.
Yáng Bǎo'ān, former Prefect of Xìn Prefecture, was dispatched to garrison Báixià.
On the *wùyín* day,
Fán Yì, Central Leader of the Army, was appointed General Who Guards the West, and Grand Administrator of all land and water forces of Jīng, Yǐng, Bā, and Wǔ Prefectures.
In the spring of the first month of the twelfth year, on the *wùxū* day,
Rèn Zhōng, Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard, was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Prefect of Nányù Prefecture,
overseeing military defenses along the river.
In the third month, on the *rénchén* day,
Lúlíng Wáng Bórén, General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed General Who Assists the Left and Central Leader of the Army.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Lù Shàn, Left Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, passed away.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Hédōng Wáng Shūxiàn, General of Upholding Might, was appointed Prefect of Nánxú Prefecture.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
there was a great prayer for rain.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
it rained.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Jìn'ān Wáng Bógōng, General of the Army Adviser and Right Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
In the sixth month, on the *rénxū* day,
a great wind damaged the central gate of Gāomén.
In the autumn of the eighth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,

Sīmă Xiāonán, Zhōu Emissary with Credentials, Pillar of the State, Grand Administrator of Yún Prefecture, and Duke of Xíngyáng Commandery, submitted with the nine prefectures of Yún, Suí, Wēn, Yìng, Tǔ, Shùn, Miăn, Huán,
and the eight garrisons of Lǔshān, Zèngshān, Dùnyáng, Yìngchéng, Píngjìng, Wǔyáng, Shàngmíng, and Xùnshuǐ.
He was enfeoffed as Duke of Suí Commandery,
and granted a set of drum and wind instruments and a set of female musicians.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an imperial edict commanded Fán Yì, General Who Guards the West, to further oversee the military affairs of Miăn and Hàn.
Rèn Zhōng, General Who Pacifies the South and Prefect of Nányù Prefecture, was dispatched to lead troops to Lìyáng;
Chén Huìjì, Palace Attendant and General Who Exceeds Martial Prowess, was appointed Front Army Commander-in-Chief
to advance to Nánliùyǔn Prefecture.
On the *wùchén* day,
Sīmă Xiāonán, newly appointed Minister of Works, was made Grand Administrator-in-Chief of all land and water forces.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Chúnyú Líng, Palace Attendant, captured Línjiāng Commandery.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Lǔ Guǎngdá, General of Martial Wisdom, captured Guōmò City.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
there was heavy incessant rain.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Chúnyú Líng captured Yòuzhōu City.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Liú Xiănguāng, Zhōu Grand Administrator of Línjiāng, led his troops to submit.
That night,
there was a sound in the southeast sky,
like wind and water clashing,
which stopped after three nights.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Ānlù Commandery was renamed Nánsī Prefecture.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Zhōu general Wáng Yánguì led troops to reinforce Lìyáng.
Rèn Zhōng attacked and defeated them,
capturing Yánguì and others alive.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Cáo Yào, a righteous leader in Zhōu's Guǎnglíng, led his troops to submit.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
there was heavy hail and thunder.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I rule over the four seas,
toiling from dawn till dusk,
aspiring to achieve perfect governance,
but have not yet reached this path.
Moreover, military expeditions are frequent,
and military expenses are particularly burdensome.
Fodder and provisions are transported,
but taxes cannot be collected.
The drought in summer harmed agriculture,
especially in the capital region.
The people lost their means of support,
This means that governance and laws are not in order,
and yin and yang are out of balance.
The common people suffer from hunger,
how can the ruler be sufficient?
Reflecting on this,
the blame lies with me.
It is fitting to extend beneficence
to all commoners.
Therefore, for the ten commanderies of Dānyáng, Wúxīng, Jìnlíng, Jiànxīng, Yìxīng, Dōnghăi, Xìnyì, Chénliú, and Jiānglíng,
The poll tax reduction shall be deferred to the autumn harvest of next year."
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Hédōng Wáng Shūxiàn, General of Upholding Might and Prefect of Nánxú Prefecture, passed away.
In the spring of the first month of the thirteenth year, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Chúnyú Liáng, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister with Independent Office, was appointed Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left;
Póyáng Wáng Bóshān, General of the Central Guard and Protector-General, was granted the title Minister with Independent Office under his current designation;
Xīn'ān Wáng Bógù, General Who Guards the Right and Libationer of the Directorate of Education, was appointed Prefect of Yáng Prefecture;
Jìn'ān Wáng Bógōng, General of the Army Adviser and Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Left Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs;
Xú Líng, General Who Pacifies the Right and Governor of Dānyáng, was appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat
and concurrently Prince's Tutor;
On the *gēngyín* day,
Yídū Wáng Shūmíng, General of Light Chariots and Minister of the Imperial Household, was appointed Prefect of Nánxú Prefecture.
In the second month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
an imperial edict bestowed titles and ranks upon Tián Guăng, Zhōu Grand General of Sīmă Xiāonán's command, and others, each according to their status.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage personally plowed the sacrificial field.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *yǐsì* day,
Shǐxīng Commandery of Héng Prefecture was divided to form Dōnghéng Prefecture,
and Héng Prefecture became Xīhéng Prefecture.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Fán Yì, former General Who Guards the West, was appointed Central Protector-General.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Fán Yì, newly appointed Central Protector-General, was appointed Protector-General.
In the autumn of the ninth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
at night,
a great wind came from the northwest,
unroofing houses and uprooting trees,
with great thunder and hail.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Máo Xǐ, Palace Attendant and Governor of Dānyáng, was appointed Minister of Personnel.
Fán Yì, Protector-General, was appointed General Who Guards the West and Prefect of Jīng Prefecture.
Póyáng Commandery was renamed Wú Prefecture.
On the *rényín* day,
the kingdom of Dāndān sent envoys to offer local products.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
a comet was seen.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Shěn Kè, General Who Assists the Right and Minister of the Imperial Household, was appointed General of the Army.
In the spring of the fourteenth year, in the first month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Gāozōng was unwell.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he passed away in the Xuānfú Diàn,
at the age of fifty-three.
His testamentary edict stated:
"Since I became ill,
it has not yet been ten days,
and medicine has not cured it.
It has already become a critical illness.
The end and my destiny are fixed;
what more can be said?
However, I have reigned over the world
for fourteen years.
Though it is said 'repose well,' I have truly not reposed well,
being cautious day by day.
I understood the heavy burden of the ancestral temples
and recognized the difficulty of the royal enterprise.
Yet the frontiers are plagued with many troubles,
and the common people are not yet settled.
I had hoped to pacify the four seas
and encompass the eight wildernesses,
but my ambition cannot be fulfilled,
leaving regret in the netherworld.
Crown Prince Shúbǎo, as the legitimate heir,
is in the prime of his youth and character.
He will inherit the grand foundation of the throne,
and the state will have a master.
All dukes, ministers, civil and military officials, both inside and outside the court,
should exert their full efforts
and exhaust their strength.
Send off the departed and serve the new ruler,
demonstrating utmost loyalty and integrity.
When holding office and fulfilling duties,
lend support and assistance.
It is essential to be harmonious
and not violate my wishes.
As for all funeral arrangements,
they should be kept simple and frugal.
Gold and silver ornaments
need not be placed in the tomb.
All burial objects
should be made of pottery.
Only let them be simple and conform to propriety,
not extravagant and contrary to measure.
Replacing months with days [mourning period]
already has a common rule;
the system for ending public mourning
shall entirely follow old regulations.
All officials in their posts
should attend court once every three days.
Governors of prefectures and commanders of garrisons in the four directions,
and the five ranks of marquises,
each should guard their respective positions
and are all to refrain from rushing to the capital."
In the second month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
he was given the posthumous title Xiàoxuān Huángdì,
and the temple name Gāozōng.
On the *guǐsì* day,
he was buried in Xiǎnníng Líng.
When Gāozōng was still a prince,
he possessed great capacity and strategic ability.
Upon ascending the throne,
he truly fulfilled the expectations of both heaven and man.
During the chaos and decline of the Liáng dynasty,
the territory of Huáinán was entirely absorbed by Qí.
In the early years of Gāozōng's Tàijiàn era,
he was determined to recover the old territory.
So he employed brilliant strategies
and dispatched armies according to military law.
Victories in battle and successful conquests
followed one after another, with reports of triumph.
He thus recovered the invaded lands,
his achievements were truly splendid.
When Zhōu destroyed Qí,
it took advantage of the victory to seize territory,
even reaching the banks of the Jiāng River.
The historian says: Gāozōng possessed a broad and magnanimous character,
and truly had the qualities of a monarch.
Shìzǔ knew that his eldest son was benevolent but weak,
and could not be entrusted with the imperial throne.
Gāozōng's position was akin to that of Jī Dàn,
and Shìzǔ's sentiment was like that towards Tàibó.
When he became ill,
all important matters were entrusted to him.
Upon inheriting the throne,
he managed all affairs of state impartially.
He appointed generals and dispatched armies,
conquering the land of Huáinán,
expanding territory,
and securing the borders.
He reigned for over ten years,
with great ambition but also a tendency to be overly relaxed.
The defeat at Lǚliáng (where his) army was destroyed
was a great loss of troops.
The weakening of the Jiāngzuǒ region
was due to this.
Alas!
His virtue did not match his literary accomplishments,
and his wisdom did not equal his military prowess.
Although success and failure were his own responsibility,
he lacked strategies to repel the enemy.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals VI: The Last Emperor
The Last Emperor's personal name was Shúbǎo,
his courtesy name was Yuánxiù,
and his childhood name was Huángnú.
He was Gāozōng's eldest legitimate son.
He was born in Jiānglíng in the eleventh month of the *wùyín* day of the second year of Chéngshèng of Liáng.
The following year,
Jiānglíng fell, and Gāozōng relocated to Guānyòu,
leaving the Last Emperor in Rángchéng.
In the third year of Tiānjiā,
he returned to the capital,
and was established as the Heir Apparent to the King of Ānchéng.
In the first year of Tiānkāng,
he was appointed General of Níngyuǎn,
and staff were assigned to him.
In the second year of Guāngdà,
he became a Central Clerk to the Crown Prince,
and soon thereafter was promoted to Palace Attendant,
with other duties remaining as before.
In the first month of the *jiǎwǔ* day of the first year of Tàijiàn,
he was established as Crown Prince.
In the fourteenth year, in the first month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Gāozōng passed away.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Shǐxīng Wáng Shúlíng committed rebellion,
and was executed.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Crown Prince ascended the imperial throne in the Tàijí Qián Diàn.
An edict stated:
"Heaven has sent misfortune;
the Great Departed Emperor suddenly abandoned the myriad states.
Clutching and wailing, throwing oneself to the ground in grief,
there is no way to reach him.
I, in my sorrow and loneliness,
inherit the precious mandate.
It is like crossing a great river,
not knowing how to reach the other shore.
I must rely on all the dukes
to assist my insignificance.
I wish to spread the departed's virtue
and extend it to the myriad people,
so that all, far and near,
may experience renewal.
Therefore, there shall be a great amnesty throughout the realm.
All civil and military officials in their posts, and those who are filial, fraternal, and diligent in agriculture and serve as heirs to their fathers,
shall all be granted one rank of nobility.
Orphans, the elderly, the widowed, and the solitary who cannot support themselves
shall be granted five *hú* of grain and two bolts of silk per person."
On the *guǐhài* day,

Palace Attendant, General of the Guard of the Van, Dānyáng Administrator, Chángshā Wáng Shújiān was made General of Agile Cavalry, Grandee of the Palace with Equivalent Privileges, and Governor of Yángzhōu.
Right Guard General Xiāo Móhē was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Nánxúzhōu.
General who Guards the West, Governor of Jīngzhōu Fán Yì was promoted to General who Conquers the West.
General who Pacifies the South, Governor of Yùzhōu Rèn Zhōng was promoted to General who Guards the South.
General of the Guards Shěn Kè was made Special Advanced Official, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness with Gold and Purple.
General who Pacifies the West Lǔ Guǎngdá was promoted to General who Pacifies the West.
General of Benevolent Might, Governor of Fēngzhōu Zhāng Dàbǎo was made Central Protector of the Army.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Empress was honored as Empress Dowager,
and her palace was named Hóngfàn.
On the *jǐngyín* day,
General of Champion Might, Jìnxī Wáng Shúwén was made General who Spreads Benevolence and Dānyáng Administrator.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
his younger brother Shúzhòng was established as King of Shǐxīng,
to offer sacrifices to Zhāoliè Wáng.
On the *jǐsì* day,
his consort, Lady Shěn, was established as Empress.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
his imperial younger brother Shúyǎn was established as King of Xúnyáng.
His imperial younger brother Shúshèn was established as King of Yuèyáng.
His imperial younger brother Shúdá was established as King of Yìyáng.
His imperial younger brother Shúxióng was established as King of Bāshān.
His imperial younger brother Shúyú was established as King of Wǔchāng.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Palace Attendant, General of the Central Right, Grandee of the Palace with Equivalent Privileges, Póyáng Wáng Bóshān was promoted to Grand General of the Central Right.
Army Advisor General, Left Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, Jìn'ān Wáng Bógōng was promoted to General of the Guard of the Van and Palace Attendant.
General of the Guard of the Right, Central Leader of the Army, Lúlíng Wáng Bórén was promoted to General who Pacifies the Van.
General who Guards the South, Governor of Jiāngzhōu, Yùzhāng Wáng Shúyīng was promoted to General who Conquers the South.
General who Pacifies the South, Governor of Xiāngzhōu, Jiàn'ān Wáng Shúqīng was promoted to General who Pacifies the South.
Palace Attendant, Central Secretariat Director, General who Guards the Right Xú Líng was made Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left,
and concurrently Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
a grand Wúshè assembly was held in the Tàijí Qián Diàn.
In the third month, on the day of Xīnhài,
an imperial edict stated:
“To personally promote and encourage [agriculture],
its righteousness is clearly shown in previous classics.
To reward diligent farmers,
this matter is manifest in past pronouncements.
This is indeed what the nation's reserves rely on,
and what the people's lives depend on.
Prosperity or hardship, rise or fall,
none is not influenced by it.
As for levying taxes, it has been so since ancient times;
transporting grain is an old practice.
Fertile lands are valued at ten gold,
while barren lands require three [re]cultivations.
Since fertile and barren lands differ,
the yields also vary.
Fraud and deceit increase daily,
and records are altered annually.
‘Inspectors of rice fields’ [Dàotián Shǐzhě]
were established in the Western Jīng [Xījīng] era;
severe penalties for dishonesty
were heard of in the Eastern Hàn [Dōnghàn].
Elderly farmers fear being interrogated,
and corrupt officials use this to abuse the law.
They abandon their ploughs in groups,
and associate with idlers.
This enduring hindrance and harm
is truly lamentable.
Now, the spring warmth is in season,
and the rich moisture penetrates the earth.
It is fitting to begin spring ploughing
in expectation of autumn harvests.
As for newly opened fields and furrows,
and newly cleared wilderness,
their extent should not be measured,
and all taxes on them are to be suspended and remitted.
Long-abandoned private lands
are all permitted to be claimed and cultivated.
Public lands left wild
may also be freely cultivated.
If good prefects teach farming,
and honest people bring wine [to celebrate],
and there are such diligent supervisors,
they should be discussed for rewards and promotions.
Externally, this can be promulgated as a regulation
to accord with Our intention.”
On the day of Guǐhài,
an imperial edict stated:
“As for governing the nation and administering the land,
nurturing the people for generations,
although reforms and changes may differ,
and tightening or relaxing measures vary,
it is always by seeking out talented individuals,
even those of humble origins,
to be used like seasoning for soup,
thus making the great edifice [of the state] flourish.
Both the most sagacious rulers and those of average ability
have followed this method.
We, being of meager virtue,
succeeded to this great destiny.
Although grief and sorrow are upon Us,
and Our thoughts are confused,
the responsibility for the ancestral altars and the state is heavy,
and the affairs of the common people are numerous.
We cannot rest idly by,
nor dare forget about bringing peace and aid.
We contemplate how to elevate and make manifest outstanding talents,
to properly equip the government.
But Our night dreams are in vain,
and We have frequently consulted historians and diviners.
No one like Wǔ Jiù [Wǔ Jiù] has come,
()nor has anyone like Bā Néng [Bā Néng] arrived.
Therefore, We ponder from dawn,
and endure anxiety day and night.
Is it that those who 'eat jade and cook cinnamon' [i.e., are wealthy and live in luxury]
have no means to make themselves known?
Or do those 'harboring treasures within their country' [i.e., possessing talent]
all wish to cultivate their own virtue in isolation?
All internal and external officials, of the ninth rank and above,
should each recommend one person,
to fulfill the purpose of collective selection.
Moreover, it is truly difficult to secure complete preparedness,
but easy to commend strengths.
The uses, whether great or small,
should be clearly stated where they can be applied.
Do not be like 'Nán Jī [Nán Jī] and Běi Dǒu [Běi Dǒu]' [i.e., have a name without substance].
Should there be those who possess ability and rely on their spirit,
but are suppressed and overlooked by their contemporaries,
who compose ‘guest plays’ [bīn xì] to pity themselves,
and write ‘guest taunts’ [kè cháo] to console their ambition—
in a person's life,
it is truly difficult to find an opportune moment.
Such people should also leave their 'hidden valleys'
and soar on this 'heavenly path.'
They should approach the bronze [gate] to observe the state,
and look towards the golden horse [statue] to come to court.
They shall then adapt to their circumstances,
and be disciplined by rules and measures.”
Another imperial edict stated:
“In ancient times, sagacious empresses governed the people,
and wise kings ruled the realm.
Although their virtue was praised as vast and profound,
and their brilliance illuminated all,
they still humbled themselves to solicit advice,
and lowered their demeanor to seek the Way.
They consulted extensively with high officials [Yuè Mù],
and listened to the common people [Yú Tái].
Thus, their governance was like that of divine beings,
and their affairs were without regret or fault.
We have succeeded to this great legacy,
and wish to promote great undertakings.
We constantly fear that the 'nine layers' [i.e., the imperial palace] are too deep,
and Our hearing from all quarters is not broad enough.
We desire to hear excellent advice,
without tiring Our feet;
if We encounter a direct rebuke in court,
We will not fear 'touching the scales' [i.e., provoking anger].
However, soft words
may be heard from those in office,
and unspoken criticism
may be hidden among colleagues.
This is not how to promote impartial governance
and illuminate the imperial reign.
All internal and external ministers, civil and military officials,
if you possess wisdom to encompass political strategies,
and your hearts are skilled in governance,
to remedy the sufferings of the people's customs,
and to discern the strictness or leniency of laws and prohibitions,
each should present loyal and upright advice,
without any concealment or evasion.
We will humbly listen and accept,
choosing what is good and acting upon it,
hoping to deeply understand the people's sentiments
and rectify Our royal standards.”
On the day of Jǐsì,
Shìzhōng, Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè, and newly appointed Yìqián Jiāngjūn, Jìn'ān Wáng Bó Gōng [Jìn'ān Wáng Bó Gōng] was made Ānnán Jiāngjūn and Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Newly appointed Yìzuǒ Jiāngjūn, Yǒngyáng Wáng Bó Zhì [Yǒngyáng Wáng Bó Zhì] was made Shàngshū Púyè.
Zhōnghùjūn Zhāng Dà Bǎo [Zhāng Dà Bǎo] was made Fēngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In summer, fourth month, on the day of Jǐngshēn,
the Imperial Prince Yǒngkāng Gōng Yìn [Yǒngkāng Gōng Yìn] was established as the Crown Prince.
A grant of one rank of nobility was bestowed upon all throughout the realm who had lost their fathers.
Kings, dukes, and those below them were granted silk and cloth, each differing according to their rank.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
“We govern the realm,
and nurture the black-haired people.
We wish to bring peace and aid to the shallow and frivolous,
and abolish extravagant and excessive expenses.
Luxury and extravagance, being contrary to moderation,
should indeed be prevented and suppressed.
All things like engraved gold and silver foils,
and sundry items such as artificial figures of people and colorful flowers made of earth and wood,
as well as cloth and silk of short width, narrow length, or light and sparse weave,
all waste wealth and impede industry,
and especially cause harm and trouble.
Furthermore, Buddhist monks and nuns, and Daoist priests
who engage in heretical and unorthodox practices,
not adhering to their scriptures and precepts,
as well as popular licentious sacrifices, ominous books, and various strange matters among the people—
these should be thoroughly regulated,
and all strictly prohibited.”
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
an imperial edict stated:
“In previous years, We subdued the Huái [Huái] and Sì [Sì] regions,
and subsequently reached Qīng [Qīng] and Xú [Xú].
The local chieftains there
all offered their sincere allegiance,
sending relatives
to serve as hostages.
Now, their former territories have been lost,
again becoming foreign lands.
North and South are separated by distance,
and they have not been able to reunite.
We think of their separation,
and feel profound affection for them.
Barbarians are Our people;
this matter is one.
Why should they alone be criticized and prohibited,
causing them to be separated?
Therefore, immediately inspect those at the Rènzǐ Guǎn [Rènzǐ Guǎn] and Dōng Guǎn [Dōng Guǎn],
as well as those who are under guarantee and reside outside.
All shall be granted clothing and provisions,
and supplied with wine and food,
so they may return to their hometowns.
If their destination is far and obstructed,
send boats and armed escorts to ensure their safe arrival.
If any have already entered officialdom or have other reasons not to leave,
their wishes shall also be respected.”
In the sixth month, on the first day, Guǐyǒu,
Míngwēi Jiāngjūn, Tōngzhí Sànqí Chángshì Sūn Yáng [Sūn Yáng] was made Zhōnghùjūn.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day of Xīnwèi,
a great amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
In this month,
the water of the Jiāng [Jiāng] River turned red like blood,
from the capital to Jīngzhōu [Jīngzhōu].
In the eighth month, on the night of Guǐwèi,
there was a sound in the sky like wind and water striking each other.
The night of Yǐyǒu was also like this.
On the day of Jǐngxū,
Shǐchíjié, Dūdū Yuánjiāng Zhū Jūnsì, Ānxī Jiāngjūn Lǔ Guǎngdá [Lǔ Guǎngdá] was made Ānzuǒ Jiāngjūn.
In the ninth month, on the Jǐngwǔ day,
a Wúfàng Dàhuì (Great Unrestricted Assembly) was held at the Tàijí Diàn (Palace of Supreme Ultimate).
The Emperor renounced his body (she shen) and his imperial carriage and robes,
and granted a general amnesty to the empire.
On the night of the Xīnhài day,
in the northeast sky, there was a sound like insects flying,
gradually moving to the northwest.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen during the day.
On the Jǐngyín day,

Chángshā Wáng Shújiān (Prince Shújiān of Chángshā) was appointed Sīkōng (Minister of Works), holding the titles of Piàojì Jiāngjūn (General of Agile Cavalry) and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (Chancellor with the same privileges as the Three Ducal Ministers), and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Yángzhōu).

Yùzhāng Wáng Shúyīng (Prince Shúyīng of Yùzhāng), who was Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Conquers the South) and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Jiāngzhōu), was confirmed in his current rank and appointed Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
In the first year of Zhìdé, in spring, in the first month, on the Rénwǔ day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, being of meager virtue,
have succeeded to the grand foundation.
My grief and anxiety are profound,
illness and affliction entwine me.
My methods for guiding the populace are few,
and my governance of those below is without calculation.
My fear is like treading on thin ice,
my trepidation like driving a decaying chariot.
Yet the four seasons flow quickly,
and the three luminaries arrive swiftly.
Gentry in robes and sashes line the steps,
jade and silk fill the court.
All things are not new,
and the seasonal order seems old.
I deeply contemplate the virtues of my predecessors,
and eternally long for those past times.
Facing the palace gates, my heart chokes,
and looking at the imperial seat, my spirit trembles.
I reflect on how to respectfully follow the legacy,
and to diligently encourage my humble self,
to nurture the nine classes (of officials),
and to bring rest to the common people,
so as to extend leniency and simplicity,
and to accord with the warmth of spring.
A general amnesty for the empire is granted,
and the fifteenth year of Tàijiàn is changed to the first year of Zhìdé."

Yùzhāng Wáng Shúyīng (Prince Shúyīng of Yùzhāng), who was Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Conquers the South), Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Jiāngzhōu), and newly appointed Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, was appointed Zhōngwèi Dàjiāngjūn (General-in-Chief of the Central Guard).
Chángshā Wáng Shújiān (Prince Shújiān of Chángshā), who was Piàojì Jiāngjūn (General of Agile Cavalry), Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Yángzhōu), was appointed Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.

Sīmǎ Xiāonàn (司馬消難), who was Zhēngdōng Jiāngjūn (General Who Conquers the East), Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Dōngyángzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Dōngyángzhōu), was promoted to Chējì Jiāngjūn (General of Chariots and Cavalry).
Jìnxī Wáng Shúwén (Prince Shúwén of Jìnxī), who was Xuānhuì Jiāngjūn (General Who Spreads Benevolence) and Dānyáng Yǐn (Administrator of Dānyáng), was appointed Yángzhōu Cìshǐ.
Rèn Zhōng (任忠), who was Zhènnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Guards the South) and Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Nányùzhōu), was appointed Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn (General Governing the Army).
Lǔ Guǎngdá (魯廣達), who was Ānzuǒ Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the Left), was appointed Píngnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the South) and Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ.
Jiāng Zǒng (江總), who was Cíbù Shàngshū (Minister of Rites), was appointed Lìbù Shàngshū (Minister of Personnel).
On the Guǐmǎo day,
Imperial Prince Shēn was enfeoffed as Shǐ'ān Wáng (Prince of Shǐ'ān).
In the second month, on the Dīngchǒu day,
Shǐxīng Wáng Shúzhòng (Prince Shúzhòng of Shǐxīng) was appointed Yángzhōu Cìshǐ.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the Wùchén day,
Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Jiāozhōu) Lǐ Yòuróng (李幼榮) presented trained elephants.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
Jìnxī Wáng Shúwén (Prince Shúwén of Jìnxī), formerly Qīngchē Jiāngjūn (General of Light Chariots) and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ, was appointed Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the Dīngmǎo day,
Chángshā Wáng Shújiān (Prince Shújiān of Chángshā), who was Piàojì Jiāngjūn (General of Agile Cavalry) and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, was appointed Sīkōng (Minister of Works).
In the ninth month, on the Dīngsì day,
in the southeast sky, there was a sound like insects flying.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the Dīngyǒu day,
Imperial Younger Brother Shúpíng was enfeoffed as Xiāngdōng Wáng (Prince of Xiāngdōng),
Shú'áo as Línhé Wáng (Prince of Línhé),
Shúxuān as Yángshān Wáng (Prince of Yángshān),
and Shúmù as Xīyáng Wáng (Prince of Xīyáng).
On the Wùxū day,

Xú Líng (徐陵), who was Shìzhōng (Palace Attendant), Ānyòu Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the Right), Zuǒguānglù Dàfū (Grandee of the Left Light and Luster), and Tàizǐ Shàofù (Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent), passed away.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
Imperial Younger Brother Shújiǎn was enfeoffed as Nán'ān Wáng (Prince of Nán'ān),
Shúchéng as Nánjùn Wáng (Prince of Nánjùn),
Shúxīng as Yuánlíng Wáng (Prince of Yuánlíng),
Shúsháo as Yuèshān Wáng (Prince of Yuèshān),
and Shúchún as Xīnxīng Wáng (Prince of Xīnxīng).
In the twelfth month, on the Jǐngchén day,
the state of Tóuhé sent envoys to present local products.
Sīkōng Chángshā Wáng Shújiān was dismissed due to a crime.
On the night of the Wùwǔ day,
the sky opened from the northwest to the southeast,
with blue and yellow colors within,
rumbling like thunder.
In the second year, in spring, in the first month, on the Dīngmǎo day,
grand envoys were dispatched to tour the customs of the provinces.
Píngnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the South) and Yùzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Yùzhōu) Lǔ Guǎngdá (魯廣達) was promoted to Ānnán Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the South).
[一０]On the Guǐsì day,
a general amnesty for the empire was granted.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the Wùzǐ day,

Shàngshū Púyè (Director of the Imperial Secretariat) Yǒngyáng Wáng Bózhì (Prince Bózhì of Yǒngyáng) was appointed Píngdōng Jiāngjūn (General Who Pacifies the East) and Dōngyángzhōu Cìshǐ (Governor of Dōngyángzhōu).
